21036.title: Managing Strategic Performance
21036.description: This subject provides an overview of employee performance management in both profit and non-profit organisations. You'll learn about the components and functions of strategic performance management systems, including 360-degree feedback and pay-for-performance. The subject also enhances your performance management skills and offers insights into the future of strategic performance management.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the theoretical foundations and contemporary developments of performance management.
Examine the alignment between individual employee performance and organisational strategy and goals to foster a high-performance culture.
Explain the relationship between performance management and other HRM functions (e.g. reward management) including the role of line managers in performance management processes.
Diagnose employee underperformance issues and critically evaluate strategies for improving performance through fair and proper procedures.

21037.title: Managing Employee Relations
21037.description: This subject familiarises you with the complexities of employment regulation in a decentralised context, focusing on Australia's current legal and regulatory framework. You'll develop practical skills in negotiation and advocacy relevant to employment relations. The subject analyses the employment relationship against the backdrop of social, economic, political, and legal factors, examining the influence and power of key institutional parties and stakeholders.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the origins and strategies of the main institutional players and the system, structure, and processes of the regulatory framework of employment relations in Australia
Explain how the shift in Australia from a centralised industrial relations system to one which is more enterprise-focused has occurred
Identify the various forms and types of enterprise agreements in Australia and their impact on work (e.g. productivity, efficiency and job satisfaction)
Apply skills in negotiation and advocacy required in achieving successful enterprise bargaining outcomes

21212.title: People and Organisations
21212.description: This subject explores how individuals operate within organisations, focusing on teamwork, leadership, motivation, organisational politics, and power dynamics. You will learn an appreciation of the importance of equity, diversity, and inclusion, and strategies for conflict resolution and effective communication with stakeholders. You will develop these skills as you self-manage your studies, work in teams, develop resilience and a framework for how to manage and successfully work in various organisational settings.
learningOutcomes: Recognise and critique contemporary debates on the role of people in organisations in wider management and organisational theory
Explain practical applications of theories and concepts of working independently and in teams
Evaluate the ethical and political consequences of leadership, managerial and worker behaviours in contemporary organisations
Apply effective communication and collaboration skills

21214.title: Business and Social Impact
21214.description: This subject examines the integration of social impact into business operations, guiding you to create businesses focused on positive social and environmental change. You'll critically assess the link between a company's mission, its activities, and their societal and environmental effects from various disciplinary angles, including accounting, economics, and marketing, as well as Indigenous and global viewpoints. You'll explore the challenges and opportunities of leveraging market forces for economic and social value creation. Through purpose-learning tasks, you'll craft your mission, empowering you as a future business leader to contribute to a more equitable and sustainable society.
learningOutcomes: Debate issues of social impact and sustainability, summarising knowledge from a range of business disciplines
Apply problem solving methodologies to evaluate existing business social impact initiatives
Critically reflect on what it means to be a responsible business leader

21227.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship
21227.description: This subject equips you with an understanding of the key theories and practices driving innovation in organisations. You'll learn to identify and apply various types of innovation, evaluating strategies and systems for managing it. Covering innovation in diverse contexts, from large firms to startups, you'll develop skills to strategically analyse and organise innovation in complex environments. Additionally, you'll gain practical insights into creating innovative business models and leveraging collaborative and digital innovation methods for value creation.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate and apply key theories, practices and tools that underpin innovation and entrepreneurship in contemporary organisations
Analyse and design organisational structures, processes and strategies to enable different types of innovation and entrepreneurship
Analyse the impact of complex and dynamic environments on innovation and entrepreneurship in contemporary organisations
Develop innovative business models that help create and capture value for organisations in novel ways

21407.title: Strategic Human Resource Management
21407.description: Dive into the world of strategic Human Resource Management (HRM) where you will explore how diverse organizations manage their people to thrive in ever-changing environments. Building on what you’ve learned in introductory HRM (21555), this subject takes you deeper into critical issues, different perspectives, and the dynamic relationship between strategy and HR. Discover how effective HR management can drive long-term success and make a real impact on an organization’s future. Get ready to think strategically and see HRM in a whole new light!
learningOutcomes: Apply the main schools of thought in strategic human resource management to organisational practice
Analyse the relationship between strategic HRM and organisational performance, including the evaluation of HRM
Assess the contemporary challenges faced by HR practitioners in establishing a strategic HRM function in relation to internal and external organisational contexts
Critically analyse ethical issues likely to arise in HRM and how these issues may be resolved
Evaluate HRM systems and practices that facilitate working with and for Indigenous persons and other cross-cultural contexts

21440.title: Management Skills
21440.description: This subject prepares you with the theoretical and practical tools needed for a successful career in management. We draw on theories such as positive psychology and positive organisational scholarship to create thriving, sustainable organisations that place a premium on employee wellbeing, optimal functioning and cultural inclusion. The subject has been designed around three themes (i) foundations of self-knowledge and understanding, (ii) managing the self at work, and (iii) managing thriving workplaces. Students interact with the subject through a variety of engaging learning techniques which emphasise active participation, collaboration and critical reflection. There is an emphasis on authentic, real-world experience with live case studies.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate a critical understanding of how theories of the self, along with current research on the self at work, can improve one’s understanding of how to build fulfilling and successful working lives and workplaces
Display evidence of personal growth and increased self-awareness in a nominated specialty area of self-development
Identify scholarly research, specifically in relation to identifying high quality, context-relevant academic sources of reference
Apply practices and principles of theories of the self, and self at work, in interactive, real-world contexts
Apply personal and leadership knowledge and skills to work with and for Indigenous peoples in a management context

21504.title: Management Capstone
21504.description: This subject integrates the knowledge from your management major, encouraging critical and creative application of theory to real-world management issues. You will analyse business cases, applying problem-solving skills to complex challenges, recognising that management problems stem from both external and internal organisational factors. Drawing on the dynamics of power and influence, you will gain practical experience in teamwork and change management. The subject includes collaborative research and reflection on individual and collective contributions to team processes.
learningOutcomes: Apply theoretical approaches to real-life management challenges
Synthesise existing theories and expertise in creative and innovative ways to solve management problems
Conduct research in teams and reflect on the student’s own and others’ contributions to team process and outcomes
apply knowledge and skills to effectively and respectfully work for and with Indigenous peoples
Demonstrate detailed understanding of management concepts and effectively communicate such concepts to an audience

21505.title: Human Resource Management (Capstone)
21505.description: This capstone subject is the culmination of your HR major. You will work on a problem-based business innovation project with a real world client and develop solutions through the application of evidence-based HRM knowledge and practices. You will utilise transferable management skills including project management, presentation design, research methods, data analysis, report writing, and teamwork. In developing your solutions, you will also have an opportunity to consider notions of organisational sustainability, gain practical insights into the role HRM plays within organisations while also enhancing your professional skills.
learningOutcomes: Critique theoretical and professional human resource management discourse to identify relevant business problems
Synthesise existing evidence to inform the development of a business innovation project
Plan and execute a business innovation project that is underpinned by a robust evidence base
Select and analyse business data in the context of existing discourse to devise human resource management plans and strategy
Present results and research findings and implications to inform stakeholder actions

21506.description: This capstone subject synthesises the knowledge acquired in the International Business major, integrating core disciplines comprehensively. It immerses you in the internationalisation process of companies, prompting critical analysis of international management practices. This enhances your professional expertise in global management. By examining current business cases and market entry strategies for international firms, you'll develop skills applicable to your future career.
learningOutcomes: Apply international business-related theoretical approaches to work practice relevant to global business environment
Engage in critical theoretical and professional discourse relevant to manage international business issues
Synthesise international business-related existing theories and expertise in creative and innovative ways
Propose and justify a market entry assessment to a company’s international expansion

21510.description: This subject provides a broad overview of the complexities involved in formulating and implementing strategy within various business environments, both domestically and internationally. You'll explore practical issues relevant to strategy including, contemporary challenges, ethical dilemmas, and sustainability issues to enable you to produce well-informed, grounded solutions to complex strategic problems. Design flexible strategic plans that enable businesses to deal with major social, environmental, technical, and economic uncertainties

21595.title: International Management Field Study
21595.description: This subject offers a study tour abroad, providing practical insights into business, management, and cultural practices of a specific country, complementing the international management theories covered in your course. It includes pre-departure briefings, business visits, talks by industry leaders, cultural tours, and free exploration time. Students often find the experience enriching, uncovering personal leadership and problem-solving skills. Note that this subject incurs additional travel costs, although group rates are negotiated to minimise expenses. The tour proceeds with sufficient enrolment, and participation requires attendance at an information session and subject coordinator approval. Express interest via email to imfs@uts.edu.au.
learningOutcomes: Discuss prevailing economic conditions and management and cultural practices in a foreign country
Analyse the pressures, problems, challenges and opportunities faced by Australian businesses in a foreign country
Develop self-awareness, and interpersonal and communication skills in a foreign culture
Examine cultural differences that might impact on building working relationships
Synthesise learning by observing the practical application of management and business theories in an overseas setting.

22320.title: Accounting for Business Combinations
22320.description:
This subject equips you with the skills necessary to apply accounting treatments for business combinations within the Australian context. While the focus is on accounting for mergers & acquisitions (M&A) and investment in associates and joint arrangements, other corporate disclosure requirements, including segments, related parties and sustainability, are also covered. You will develop a thorough understanding of the institutional and legal frameworks governing accounting practices, enhancing your ability to interpret and adhere to current standards.

Learning unfolds through weekly pre-recorded lecture materials that introduce technical and theoretical concepts, supplemented by practical examples. This is followed by face-to-face interactive workshops where you will engage in class discussions of demonstration questions and case studies. It is essential that you read the lecture materials before attending the workshops. Tutorials are designed to reinforce lecture content and develop hands-on accounting skills.

You are encouraged to come prepared to discuss and solve assigned problems. As part of the assessments, you will also participate in a group project to analyse a recent M&A case to bring more real-world relevance into your learning. You will receive timely feedback through Canvas, class interactions, assessments, and forum responses.
learningOutcomes: Apply the regulations that determine accounting and reporting for economic entities
Prepare financial statements for economic entities that accounts for subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures, and provides segment information
Implement accounting and reporting techniques to non-routine circumstances and new events
Discuss, in written form, the appropriate accounting treatment applicable in the given circumstances.

23002.title: Market Design
23002.description:
This subject equips you with the knowledge and ability to analyse strategic decision-making, a new area of economic science. You will see how this changes our understanding of the way markets work and then you’ll use this understanding to explore the rules that govern markets and how they can be designed to produce better social outcomes. The markets you study will include online auctions, government auctioning of natural resources, matching markets (for example, where students must be matched to classes or schools, medical patients to hospitals, or kidneys to recipients), health care markets and electricity markets.

Your learning will combine lectures with tutorials, fostering an interactive environment in which theory meets practice, preparing you for the challenges of working in real markets and helping to improve their operation and performance.
learningOutcomes: understand the field of market design, its applications and the associated engineering concerns
develop reasonable solutions to real work market design problems and evaluated their theoretical performance
use economic theory, experiments and empirical analysis to assess market rules and institutions

23021.title: Labour Economics
23021.description:
This subject equips you with the analytical tools to understand and evaluate the functioning of labour markets, particularly in Australia. You'll learn to apply economic theories to explain employer and employee behaviour, and analyse labour market outcomes such as wages and employment. You will critically assess the impact of labour market policies and shocks - such as minimum wage laws, anti-discrimination regulations, family-friendly policies, education subsidies and technological changes- on labour markets.

Your learning journey will comprise interactive lectures and tutorials, where you'll engage with real-world scenarios and policy debates. Online resources, including lecture materials and discussion forums, support your studies, allowing you to download content, complete assessments, and collaborate with peers and lecturers. Expect prompt feedback on weekly tasks and comprehensive reviews of major assignments to enhance your understanding of labour markets.
learningOutcomes: describe institutions and historical trends relevant to Australian labour markets as well as sources of individual differences in wages and employment
apply formal microeconomic frameworks to analyse a range of labour market phenomena
critically evaluate government policies with respect to their effects on wages and employment.

23510.title: Economic Inequality
23510.description:
This subject will help you develop an understanding of the nature and causes of inequalities in wealth and income that characterise the world. You’ll learn about global as well as local dimensions of inequality, and you’ll explore the nature of disparities between various population sub-groups including indigenous peoples, and how these disparities change over time.

You'll learn to measure inequality, to differentiate between outcome and opportunity disparities, and to use economic theories in explaining these phenomena. Factors such as capital, labour, technological change, globalisation, education, financialisation and institutional structures will all become concepts at your disposal to analyse the drivers of inequality. Additionally, you'll assess government policies aimed at reducing inequality. Your learning combines online lectures, self-study and interactive tutorials, where you'll engage with case studies and group discussions to reinforce your knowledge.
learningOutcomes: Discuss the relationships between equity, equality of outcomes and opportunities, and poverty
Compare and contrast the ways in which inequality can be measured
Describe how inequality has evolved over time within and between countries and sub-populations and its consequences for those countries and sub-populations
Discuss the determinants of various types of inequality
Analyse how various government policies may be used to mitigate against the various types of inequality and their consequences
Critically evaluate the claim that rising inequality is inevitable

Active participation in tutorials and online forums will facilitate collaboration with staff and other students, and through these activities you’ll receive regular feedback on the progress of your learning, ensuring that you develop a sound understanding of markets and the macroeconomy.

Collaboratively and effectively communicate critical evaluations of economic phenomena in writing, enhancing teamwork skills by developing and presenting analyses as a cohesive group
Critically reflect how Indigenous experiences intersect with economic policies to inform education strategies that support Indigenous communities

23569.title: Economic Growth, Development and Sustainability
23569.description: This subject will help you explore the nature of economic growth, the various explanations economists have offered for the process of growth, and the relationship between growth and economic development, particularly in poorer countries. You will consider how economic growth has played such an important role in raising living standards in a number of countries around the world since the industrial revolution and analyse why the effects of that growth have been so unevenly distributed. You will also acquire the conceptual tools to assess recent calls for a re-think of the emphasis placed on economic growth given the link between growth and climate change. You will examine the potential limits on growth and consider what a sustainable and globally just approach to growth might look like by paying careful attention to the development needs of poorer nations.
learningOutcomes: Explain the impacts of unequal material prosperity
Analyse the determinants of economic growth and its relationship to development and sustainability
Evaluate the range of policies designed to foster economic growth

25300.title: Fundamentals of Business Finance
25300.description: The subject introduces and develops the core technical and theoretical concepts of Finance and illustrates their application to practical financial decision-making problems. Two crucial concepts are introduced: (1) the time-value of money (TVM); and (2) financial risk. TVM techniques are applied to the valuation and management of financial instruments, such as annuities, perpetuities and amortising loans, and to financial securities, such as stocks and bonds. Different ways of measuring financial risk are considered and the fundamental relationship between risk and return is demonstrated empirically and explained. TVM and risk analysis techniques are applied to investment and financing decision problems in a Corporate Finance context. In particular, students learn how firms decide which projects to invest in and how they choose to raise the capital to fund those investments.
learningOutcomes: describe the principles and objectives of financial decision-making
apply time-value of money techniques to the valuation of financial instruments and financial securities
demonstrate an understanding of financial risk, its measurement, and its relationship to return
evaluate a corporate investment proposal and provide a recommendation to accept or reject it

25410.description: As the capstone for the Finance Major, this subject integrates theory and practice, enhancing decision-making skills across various financial contexts. Through case studies and real-world data, you'll navigate the complexities of personal wealth, investment and risk management, corporate finance, capital structure, executive pay, venture capital, and ethics. This hands-on approach prepares you for practical financial decision-making.
learningOutcomes: Identify the sources of risk in a financial decision
Determine the cash flow implications of a financial decision
Compare the financing alternatives for a business or project
Discuss the roles of ethics and agency costs in financial decisions
Assess a business proposal and recommend a course of action

You'll develop technical skills to analyse and value equities, debts, and alternative investments, and learn to construct, manage, and evaluate asset portfolios for both individual and institutional investors.

Recommend whether to buy or sell shares in a company by interpreting the reports of financial analysts

25557.title: Applied Corporate Finance
25557.description: This subject provides a practical introduction to the theory and practice of corporate finance. You will learn how to evaluate projects and make investment decisions, how to estimate a firm's cost of capital and determine its optimal capital structure, how to choose between buying and leasing long-term assets, and how to manage short-term assets like cash and inventory. You will also learn how firms distribute capital to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases, how they raise capital by issuing shares and taking on debt, as well as the ins and outs of mergers and acquisitions and corporate governance.
learningOutcomes: Assess key issues in corporate finance, with a view to making optimal investment, financing and payout decisions.
Evaluate an investment proposal or a financing proposal, and prepare a recommendation for corporate executives.
Work collaboratively in a group to evaluate corporate financial data and corporate social responsibility reports, with the aim of formulating and presenting an investment recommendation.
Make judgements about the propriety and effectiveness of corporate social responsibility projects and Indigenous outreach initiatives.

25574.title: Commercial Bank Management
25574.description: This subject critically examines commercial banking management, risk, regulation, and performance, highlighting the role of banks in financial intermediation and the economy. You'll explore the structure of the financial system and the challenges of managing banks, applying theory to real-world scenarios from various stakeholder perspectives. While centred on commercial banks, the concepts also apply to non-bank institutions. You'll apply your knowledge through assignments analysing real financial institutions and their lending and deposit risks.
learningOutcomes: Explain the major activities products and services provided of commercial banks
Discuss the management of risk related activities undertaken by commercial banks
Illustrate the role of commercial banks in the financial services market
Evaluate the role of commercial banks in the function of the economy.
Apply financial management knowledge to banking practice
Appraise action in commercial banking situation

25602.title: Ethics in Finance
25602.description: Ethical practices foster public trust and market efficiency, which benefits stakeholders and boosts investor confidence. This subject provides a framework for ethical conduct in finance, centred on the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct. By studying a collection of scandals that arose from ethical misconduct, you will understand the critical role of ethics in financial institutions and the importance of personal integrity for finance professionals.
learningOutcomes: Explain the major intellectual theories of ethics as a basis for the analysis and resolution of ethical dilemmas in finance

Critically examine ethical standards and issues of questionable professional conduct in finance by addressing topical issues related to ethics in investment decisions, financial markets, and financial services

Relate ethical principles to the financial theory of the firm, stakeholder theory, takeovers, corporate social responsibility and governance, international businesses, machine learning and artificial intelligence

Analyse, interpret and apply the CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct and recommend practices and procedures designed to prevent violations of ethical and professional practices related to financial analysis, investment management, and financial market trading

Discuss financial risks and how to manage them
Illustrate the use of derivatives in the management of financial risks and in exploring financial arbitrage
Analyse and formulate derivative trading positions and strategies for financial trading purposes

25624.title: Financial Metrics for Decision Making
25624.description: This subject introduces financial decision-making and the impact of big data. You'll learn to make informed decisions in management finance, personal savings, and investments. Starting with the traditional rational belief and utility maximisation paradigm, the course incorporates psychological research, acknowledging irrational beliefs, alternative preferences, and cognitive limits. You'll calculate financial metrics, apply decision-making rules, identify common biases, and explore techniques to mitigate them, using real data for practical understanding.
learningOutcomes: Describe various decision-making techniques and explain the roles of financial metrics, utility theory, prospect theory and systematic biases in financial decision-making
Recommend a financial decision based on data, using appropriate financial and statistical concepts and techniques
Identify cognitive biases and analyse their impact on corporate behaviour and asset prices

26134.title: Responsible Evidence-Based Decisions
26134.description: This subject is designed to develop students' abilities to use evidence-based reasoning to solve important problems confronting business and society at large. Statistics and data are ubiquitous in the modern corporate world. Students will learn quantitative methods essential for organisational roles across all business discipline areas. The relevance of these methods will be demonstrated with applications to a diverse set of real-world case studies. The subject will train students to be responsible users of data, emphasising ethical considerations, the strengths and limitations of analytical tools, and how to communicate statistical evidence to inform decision making, laying the foundation for further study in different business disciplines.
learningOutcomes: Apply standard statistical tools in various business decision contexts within a professionally responsible framework
Apply appropriate quantitative analytical techniques to qualify, support, select and evaluate data as information for use in business decision-making
Interpret and communicate results of quantitative analyses for business decision-making
Use a computer-based data analysis package (i.e. Excel) to critically analyse data

Discuss the importance of individuals applying ethical and socially responsible decision-making in Business practices
Critically reflect on the learning and development outcomes of the workplace experience

26776.title: Foundations of Business Analytics
26776.description: Business analytics is concerned with the use of data, quantitative analysis, predictive models and fact-based management to create value for organisations. With the tremendous growth in the amount of data being generated by organisations, government and society, it is crucial that the leaders of tomorrow understand the proper tools to be able to make evidence-based decisions. In Foundations of Business Analytics, students are provided with the foundations of business analytics, as well as an introduction to techniques and methods required to undertake practical problems. Students ultimately gain the necessary knowledge to initiate and conduct small scale business analytics projects and professionally communicate their findings to a diverse set of stakeholders.
learningOutcomes: Explain the background of business analytics
Demonstrate methods to locate, prepare and analyse data in order to be able to make predictions
Communicate the results of a business analytics project
Relate ethical principles to the collection, storage and use of data by business and government

31005.title: Machine Learning
31005.description: This subject equips you with the skills to apply machine learning, a key driver of innovation across various industries, by teaching you to program and analyse intelligent systems that learn from data. You will develop a clear understanding of both foundational and advanced algorithms through practical exercises and theoretical study. Your learning experience will blend active engagement with real-world applications, particularly in artificial intelligence, preparing you for immediate professional application and further exploration in the field.
learningOutcomes: Describe the scope, limitations and application of several advanced machine learning methods. (D.1)
Use or program a machine learning method. (D.1)
Design an approach to machine learning problems in specialised domains. (C.1)
Demonstrate an understanding of the issues underlying machine learning to successfully outline an approach to solving a machine learning problem. (D.1)

31061.title: Database Principles
31061.description: This subject provides a foundational understanding of database design and implementation, focusing on relational design principles and Entity Relationship Diagrams. You will learn to interpret and develop these diagrams and access databases using Structured Query Language (SQL) for data retrieval. Additionally, the subject covers the coding skills necessary to construct a database. Preparation is essential ahead of lectures, while labs offer practical exercises for your learning, ensuring you can effectively design and query databases.
learningOutcomes: Design an Entity-Relationship (E-R) model from specifications and transform a conceptual model into corresponding logical data structures. (D.1)
Construct Structured Query Language (SQL) statements and maintain a simple database. (D.1)
Critically evaluate database designs and the role databases play in effective software applications. (C.1)
Effectively communicate database design. (E.1)
31061.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject are familiar with basic system analysis concepts and have basic software skills.

31080.title: Interactive Media
31080.description: This subject introduces you to the fundamentals of interactive media, preparing you to design and develop systems that integrate digital audio, images, animation, and video for immersive user experiences. You will gain proficiency in creative coding tools and techniques, applying them to create compelling content for various domains such as gaming, arts, and data visualisation. The emphasis is on practical application, ensuring that you can craft interactive media that captivate users in real-world scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Apply knowledge of digital sampling, storage and mapping techniques for still images, video, sound and sensor data to make appropriate design choices for interactive media applications. (D.1)
Use digital sound, image and video processing algorithms to alter digital media. (D.1)
Design and develop interactive media applications which incorporate a range of different interactive components to create effective and engaging user experiences. (C.1)
Reflect on the nature of digital media components to devise novel and effective applications and descriptions of interactive media systems. (F.1)
Provide creative and critical feedback and ask thoughtful questions of peers in a supportive and constructive manner (E.1)

31097.title: IT Operations Management
31097.description: In this subject, you will develop the skills necessary for managing resources in an information systems organisation, including hardware, software, and personnel. You will learn about resource acquisition, software development, workplace management, recruitment, training, security practices, operations management, and service level agreements. The subject also covers industry frameworks and standards such as ITIL, alongside contemporary topics like cloud computing, equipping you with a comprehensive skill set for effective IT resource management.
learningOutcomes: Identify with the scope and challenges of the role of an IT Manager. (B.1)
Analyse the responsibilities, structures and functional areas of the IT Department. (D.1)
Produce competency portfolios and service level agreements in an IT department. (C.1)
Suggest commercially viable solutions to typical challenges in an IT department. (D.1)

31241.title: Interactive 3D Animation
31241.description:
This subject delves into 3D animation for interactive applications like games or short animated productions, covering the entire production pipeline from storyboarding to animation, camera positioning, interactive control, code integration, lighting, advanced real-time rendering, and VFX.

You will actively engage in pre-production planning, practical realisation, and post-production with a game engine and a project-based approach emphasising learning by doing. This hands-on experience equips you with the skills to manage, enhance, and integrate animated components into games or to execute a complete animation project.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the theory of the design and production of 3D digital animation. (D.1)
Develop animation skills and the ability to look at motion analytically. (D.1)
Design and rig a basic character for 3D animation using appropriate processes and workflows. (C.1)
Create a character-based 3D Animation from planning stage (storyboard) to final 3D rendered short. (C.1)
31241.recommended: basic knowledge of drawing and 2D digital image processing (basic Photoshop) is useful

31245.title: Business Process and IT Strategy
31245.description:
This subject introduces you to the strategic use of information technology (IT) to enhance business processes and strategies. A major concern for businesses is finding a competitive advantage and effectively leveraging IT resources to align with business goals. For IT managers, this involves understanding and managing complex issues related to the roles of IT and IT strategy in enabling business processes and generating business benefits and competitive advantage. In this subject, we will explore theories and methods related to the value of IT. You will learn about and discuss business and strategy processes that lead to learning organisations capable of achieving sustainable competitive advantage.

Business processes and IT strategy are crucial concerns for both business and IT managers. Managing information is a critical skill for success in today's business environment. Managers need to understand their organisation's capabilities and the use of information resources. This subject aims to provide a foundation to help general business managers become knowledgeable participants in decision-making processes related to information systems (IS). By critically reviewing the contributions of IS resources in businesses and organisational settings, you will gain a contextual understanding of how IS permeates many aspects of business.

Through case studies, this subject reinforces material provided in lectures and tutorials, along with additional research and prior knowledge. It gives you the opportunity to enhance your problem-solving, critical thinking, and organisational skills as part of a group, as well as to engage in peer learning. The subject emphasises the development and assessment of real-world experience through applied and innovative tasks and team effort. You will develop the knowledge and skills required for using and managing information within an organisation, as well as essential management and communication skills.
learningOutcomes: Theorise on the impact of information systems technology in business process transformation (BPT) and strategic information systems planning (SISP) and why businesses undertake BPT or SISP to achieve sustainable competitive advantage. (B.1)
Explain the role of non-IT enablers that affect successful BPT. (B.1)
Describe the complex network of organisational issues that arise during BPT or SISP and their impact on IS and business alignment. (B.1)
Explain the need for collaboration between IS personnel and their customers to achieve satisfactory solving of complex problems. (B.1)
Present, discuss and support their analyses of issues involving business and strategy processes in learning organisations. (E.1)

31247.title: Collaborative Business Processes
31247.description: This subject provides you with a comprehensive problem-solving framework, essential for agile teams to foster creativity, critical thinking, and innovation. Starting with problem scoping, you'll gain a data-supported understanding of issues, utilising collaborative tools for knowledge sharing. You'll apply techniques like process modelling and systems thinking to generate solutions, while focusing on addressing current and emergent societal or business challenges. The subject encourages knowledge exchange and the development of practical solutions.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the roles of collaborative processes in problem solving, in the context of contemporary challenges. (B.1)
Collaboratively synthesise multiple viewpoints, and evaluate ideas to formulate “wicked problems”. (C.1)
Apply appropriate collaborative process toolsets to solve the selected problem(s). (D.1)
Evaluate formulations and solutions of peers to inform optimal outcomes. (E.1)
Use reflection strategies to enhance students’ personal contributions to the workplace. (F.1)

31248.title: Serious Games and Gamification Studio
31248.description: This subject focuses on creating serious games and gamified experiences, designed for purposes beyond entertainment such as education or training. You'll learn cutting-edge design frameworks and techniques for tailoring games to specific audiences and objectives. Working with end-users, you'll engage in co-design workshops, prototype development, playtesting, and evaluation to ensure impactful outcomes. Additionally, you'll consider the ethical implications inherent in game design.
learningOutcomes: Apply professional standards relating to Indigenous Australian contexts when designing games and serious games. (A.1)
Evaluate ethical, cultural, and societal considerations when designing a bespoke serious game or gamified experience. (B.1)
Design a game-like prototype that serves a specific purpose for a specific audience. (C.1)
Critically reflect on one’s own designs and iteratively propose alternate game-like solutions that fit a purpose and benefit an audience. (F.1)

31250.title: Introduction to Data Analytics
31250.description: This subject covers the fundamentals of data analytics, blending art and science to transform large, complex datasets into actionable insights. You will learn data preprocessing, exploration, visualization, and predictive modeling using various data analytics techniques. By connecting cutting-edge research with practical applications, this subject prepares you to undertake data mining projects, collaborate with analytics professionals, and effectively communicate your findings.
learningOutcomes: Explain the value proposition of data analytics in a business context to immediate stakeholders. (B.1)
Use data analytics techniques to derive meaningful insights from data in a business context. (C.1)
Apply data analytics techniques to explore and predict trends based on data set. (D.1)
Identify the limitations and possibilities of different data analytics methods. (D.1)
Communicate data analytics findings to immediate stakeholders. (E.1)

31251.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
31251.description: This subject equips you with the skills to design, evaluate, and implement data structures and algorithms using C++, ensuring they meet criteria for functionality and usability. You'll learn the underlying concepts, theories, and technologies essential for creating software solutions that are suitable, understandable, easy to learn, and compliant.
learningOutcomes: Apply principles of program design to the C++ language in an integrated development environment. (C.1)
Analyse data structures and algorithms principles to unstructured data and complicated problem. (D.1)
Apply data structures and algorithms principles using C++ to complicated problems. (D.1)
31251.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have prior programming experience in some language, including understanding of basic programming concepts such as variables, conditional statements, and control flow.

31257.title: Information System Development Methodologies
31257.description: This subject arms you with the techniques to navigate the complexities of information system design and development, acknowledging there's no one-size-fits-all solution. You'll learn to assess various methodologies, pinpointing their strengths and weaknesses, a critical skill for effective software project management.
learningOutcomes: Analyse key aspects of a number of Information System development methodologies to develop business Systems. (B.1)
Explain that different methodologies target different aspects of Information System development, such as requirements gathering, project management or cross-organisational development. (C.1)
Evaluate development methodologies and articulate their underlying philosophies to solve organisational Information System problems. (D.1)
Illustrate a methodology, or aspects of different methodologies to substantiate the suitability of particular circumstances. (D.1)
31257.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of the software development life cycle and systems modelling techniques

31258.title: Innovations for Global Relationship Management
31258.description: This subject explores the evolving role of the Australian computing industry, emphasising its shift towards leveraging computers for relationship maintenance, knowledge management, and innovation to gain competitive advantage. You'll examine the industry's global context, the value of IT in business, and the implications of e-commerce, customer relationship management, user modelling, outsourcing, offshoring, and legal issues in the digital economy. The subject also addresses organising business information, focusing on informal flows within organisations, and examines various work relationships, team formation, and management processes. Practical skills include using portals and other tools for customer loyalty and outsourcing collaborations.
learningOutcomes: Explain the impact and opportunities of IT within the Australian and global economic context by using computer tools such as portals, etc to maintain relationships and grow these opportunities. (B.1)

Discuss how IT adds value to business in e-commerce, relationship and knowledge management, user modelling for customer satisfaction, outsourcing, off shoring and software development by using computers for innovation that leads to competitive advantage. (B.1)
Recognise how Intellectual Property, Service Level Agreements, patents and other legal tools are involved in the formalization of relationships in IT. (D.1)
Demonstrate the attributes employers look for when hiring and comprehend how to develop these skills in the context of organisational culture and fit of the employee. (F.1)

31260.title: Fundamentals of Interaction Design
31260.description: This subject develops your ability to design, evaluate, and implement interactive systems with a human-centered approach. You'll understand human-computer interaction (HCI) and interaction design principles, learning key concepts, tools, and techniques. You'll also consider how designers' metaphors for human activity affect system usability and how human-centered design and evaluation can enhance interactive systems.
learningOutcomes: Apply a range of approaches, techniques, tools, and methods available when designing useful and usable technology. (D.1)
Design digital mockup of prototype to achieve success for usability. (C.1)
Assist people through design of interconnected solutions going beyond isolated technologies. (B.1)
31260.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of interactive technologies, design and programming skills.

31262.title: Game Design Methodologies
31262.description: This games subject trains you to be an engineer of entertainment, teaching you the essential theoretical concepts and practical methodologies for game design. You will learn to structure, document, target, and scope your game designs with further refinement through weekly iteration via playtest feedback. As part of a group, you will first learn to apply these creative theories and methods to develop a physical board game prototype before moving on to crafting a digital game using a popular game engine. While this subject is not focused on game development skills such as coding or art creation, you are encouraged to self-learn what's necessary to realise your group’s vision. Regular playtesting with peers will help refine your designs. By the subject's end, you'll have created both board and digital games, showcasing your interaction design expertise for future employment portfolios. You will be better prepared for the iterative development cycle common in later game studio subjects and the wider game industry.
learningOutcomes: Design and critique games as dynamic systems of formal and dramatic elements. (C.1)
Collaborate effectively within a group to incorporate diverse perspectives and skill sets in the design. (E.1)
Rapidly develop digital game prototypes to gather early player feedback. (D.1)
Critically reflect and act on playtest feedback during iterative designs cycles. (C.1)
31262.recommended: familiarity with computer graphics and experience with designing interactive systems

31263.title: Introduction to Computer Game Development
31263.description: This subject introduces you to game development using a commercial-grade game engine, focusing on building a strong foundation in generalisable virtual interaction simulation theory and intermediate programming problem solving skills in the Unity Game Engine. You'll become familiar with industry terminology, engine interface tools, vector and matrix maths for object transformation, and programming involving the engine API. You will be assessed on your practical skills development through weekly lab content to ensure consistent skill development over the session. You will create a classic video game over the semester, beginning with the asset creation and import into the engine, and then programming the game logic akin to the original game experience. You will also craft a level with a unique twist to allow for you to develop your creative problem-solving skills, a crucial skill for any aspiring game developer. The skills developed in this subject will prepare you to contribute effectively to group projects in future game-related subjects and subject outcomes can be utilised in an employment portfolio.
learningOutcomes: Understand foundational language and theory of game development technology. (D.1)
Apply mathematical and game programming knowledge to solve development tasks. (D.1)
Navigate the interface and codebase of an industry standard game development engine. (D.1)
Proactively identify their own knowledge gaps and establish skills in life-long learning through sourcing new knowledge to solve previously unseen intermediate problems. (F.1)
Design and implement minor variations to existing game designs. (C.1)

31264.title: Computer Graphics
31264.description: This subject equips you with problem-solving and communication skills specific to computer graphics, focusing on shape representation, manipulation, and visualisation. You will learn to design and implement 3D interactive graphics for applications such as virtual reality (VR), data visualisation, and gaming. Balancing theory and practice, you'll delve into graphical pipelines and representations and apply this knowledge using WebGL and the ThreeJS framework. You'll emerge with an understanding of the systems driving game engines and 3D animation software and the ability to create interactive 3D web applications, valuable for various studies and careers.
learningOutcomes: Implement an interactive application using ThreeJS and WebGL. (C.1)
Integrate principles of linear algebra into computer graphics applications (D.1)
Implement data structures and algorithms for 3D shape representation and real-time rendering (D.1)
Communicate design ideas, models, implementations and outcomes to a technical audience. (E.1)
Reflect on one’s own work to identify changes in practice for future projects. (F.1)
31264.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have some experience with an integrated development environment such as Visual Studio would be an advantage, but is not essential; knowledge of linear algebra (e.g. vectors, matrices and their manipulation), data structures (e.g. multi-dimensional arrays, stack) is strongly recommended; good programming skills in at least one programming language is required to successfully complete the subject.

31265.title: Communication for IT Professionals
31265.description: This core subject will highlight new ways of working, provide insights into the scope of technology, and look at considerations within the Australian context. You will learn to make decisions that impact people, community, and the environment. Through authentic experiences, you will develop skills and knowledge, providing a solid base for your continuous professional development as an IT professional. In the subject, you will complete the Engineers Without Borders Challenge, working in a team to develop solutions to real-world challenges for an Australian Aboriginal or Torres Strait Island community. You will form a team with peers, working in and outside class throughout the session on the project that you select. Your team will research the project background, refine scope and identify technological considerations. You will then ideate and prototype potential solutions that work in the community context. Finally, you will propose a fully developed design idea that benefits the partner community. In completing the challenge, you will develop multidisciplinary and professional skills including: researching skills to inform the development of design solutions; applying the design process to solve genuine humanitarian challenges; considering socio-technical issues including working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities; developing professional communications skill; and participating and leading team processes.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate an awareness of Indigenous Australian cultural, historic, and contemporary contexts in order to inform work in a complex project. (A.1)
Identify stakeholder needs and ethical considerations through the empathise design stage. (B.1)
Apply a design thinking approach to meet stakeholder needs. (C.1)
Communicate an evidence-based design solution for an IT or engineering project. (E.1)
Explain the collaboration and contributions of team planning, communication and problem-solving in developing a design solution. (E.1)

31266.title: Introduction to Information Systems
31266.description: This subject examines the integration and application of IT technology within society, business, government, and community systems, highlighting trends like increased mobility, complexity, globalisation, and networking in a data-centric world. It explores how IT technology enhances service delivery and competitiveness in a global, networked economy. You'll learn the role of information systems in business management and network formation, using real-world case studies to grasp how IS contributes to competitive advantage. The subject covers IS development, implementation, and maintenance, while also fostering team collaboration and relationship skills. Ethical, privacy, and security considerations are also addressed. You'll apply theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios, innovate, and cultivate teamwork skills.
learningOutcomes: Identify business, organizational and society environment to propose types of IS for obtaining and maintaining competitive advantage. (B.1)
Demonstrate data management approaches for implementing knowledge management systems in organisations. (D.1)
Discuss key concepts relating to telecommunication and networking. (D.1)
Describe the process of acquiring information systems and applications. (D.1)
Identify ethical issues in the IS context to propose recommendations. (B.1)

31268.title: Web Systems
31268.description: This subject is an introduction to information technology, using the web as a core case study. You will learn about the underlying hardware, software, networks and operating systems behind websites, and set up a functional website using this knowledge.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the basic concepts of hardware, software, cybersecurity, processes and the components of an Operating System including how to work on the command line and create simple scripts. (D.1)
Identify and explain the role and function of the Internet, the World Wide Web, and their components. Describe and make use of distributed applications on the Internet. (D.1)
Design and implement a simple web site to a given specification. (C.1)
31268.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have prior use of an operating system; the availity to browse and search the internet.

31269.title: Business Requirements Modelling
31269.description:
This subject focuses on modelling business requirements, emphasising the importance of understanding different perspectives of the users to enhances system quality in resolving real-world business problems. 

You'll explore contemporary requirements modelling approaches, both agile and non-agile software engineering principles, methods, tools, and techniques, to analyse business processes and model requirements via the business process models and data models as well as capture functional and non-functional requirements via agile artifacts and object-oriented models.

You'll participate in interactive and hands-on lectures, tutorials as well as team projects with real-world business problems, which will develop key skills for critical roles like Business Analyst in designing and developing innovative software systems in professional settings
learningOutcomes: Identify stakeholders, define their needs, and determine the methods to effectively capture and model business requirements in the system development process. (B.1)
Apply diverse systems analysis and design techniques to model system and user requirements and document them effectively using an Agile Software Requirements Specification (Agile SRS). (C.1)
Apply modelling and systems analysis techniques to effectively describe the operations and functionality of a business system using business process models and data models. (D.1)
Communicate the impact of individual contributions by analysing personal decisions and articulating their influence on team outcomes. (E.1)

31271.title: Database Fundamentals
31271.description:
This subject lays the foundation for effective database systems, teaching you how data is structured and managed within organizations, ensuring its usability for applications and users. You will also learn SQL for effective data retrieval and modification, enhancing your ability to work with databases in various contexts.

During the subject, you'll explore the significance and challenges of good database design and management, which underpin a strong basis for developing functional software applications. You'll enhance your skills through hands-on practicals and case study analyses, applying theoretical concepts to real-world situations.

This subject is particularly beneficial for students pursuing majors in computer science, information systems, or related fields. It prepares you for roles in database administration, software development, and data analysis.
learningOutcomes: Construct conceptual data models using appropriate database design, and data modelling principles. (C.1)
Identify data redundancy levels and their impact on database integrity and maintainability using data normalisation principles. (D.1)
Construct efficient SQL queries to retrieve and manipulate data as required. (D.1)
31271.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject are familiar with basic system analysis concepts and have basic software skills.

31272.title: Project Management and the Professional
31272.description: This subject equips you with project management skills, focusing on information systems and professional project management. You will learn about ethical standards and the organisational context of projects. You will also learn about the roles of project team members, managing time, risk, cost and communications and the value of quality. These skills are vital for university success and for success in your future career. Learning involves being part of a small project team. You will collaborate to create project documents, receiving constructive feedback to foster improvement. These activities culminate in a significant group assessment followed by a reflection on what you have learnt. You will also write a report stating the possible ethical dilemmas in a given case study and describing how industry codes may be used to suggest solutions to these dilemmas. Academic and professional language and communication skills are measured through a milestone assessment task that gauges both your subject knowledge and communication proficiency.This subject also supports the development of the Indigenous Graduate Attribute (IGA). You will engage with IGA learning modules and industry perspectives to strengthen your understanding of the ethical engagement with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and communities. These resources introduce principles such as Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC), Indigenous self‑determination, Indigenous Data Sovereignty, and reciprocity, and highlight their relevance to professional project practice.
learningOutcomes: Critically reflect on ethical principles of stakeholder engagement to work effectively with and for Indigenous Australians within project contexts. (A.1)
Explain the social impact of information technology and responsibility of IT professionals and importance of ethical codes of conduct within projects. (B.1)
Divide a project into components to explain what value that project will provide if implemented. (D.1)
Use team building skills and generic tools to plan a project. (E.1)
Collaborate in teams to create the project outcome. (E.1)
Reflect on what has been learnt and how this can feed into better outcomes for future projects. (F.1)

31275.title: Mobile Networking
31275.description: Wireless networks, including cellular, WiFi, Bluetooth, satellite, and near-field communication networks, establish pervasive connections to devices and end-users, serving as foundational technologies across virtually all industries today. This subject explores the principles and applications of wireless telecommunications and their integration with the internet. It emphasizes key concepts, infrastructure, and protocols critical to these networks, particularly their ability to support a diverse array of devices and mobility needs. The subject includes guest lectures from leading Australian telecommunications companies, offering firsthand insights into the latest cellular technologies. You will gain extensive hands-on experience by addressing real-world industry challenges and developing either emulated sensing/communication systems or working prototypes in group projects. This approach not only imparts fundamental knowledge but also equips you with practical skills applicable across numerous engineering fields. By the end of this subject, you'll have a comprehensive understanding of wireless networks, equipped to engage with advanced technologies and innovations.
learningOutcomes: Explain the concepts, techniques and protocols employed in various wireless networks to perform consulting tasks involving support roles for wireless technologies. (D.1)
Analyze the network infrastructure requirements to support mobile devices and users. (B.1)
Develop and roadshow innovative solutions for practical applications of wireless technologies. (C.1)
Evaluate and solve integrated problems in mobile networking by applying theoretical concepts, protocol standards, and case-based reasoning. (D.1)

args.text: Admission into MAJ03539 54cp Telecommunications and Electronics (MPE)

31275.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have a basic understanding of networking and telecommunication concepts.

31277.title: Routing and Switching Essentials
31277.description: Building on prior knowledge, this subject offers a deeper dive into networking. You'll develop expertise for specialisation and understand networks' influence on applications. Key skills include learning IP addressing, routing protocols and switched networks. You will be designing and implementing small to medium-sized intranets, and managing network security. You'll also evaluate the role of TCP/IP, ICMP, and other IP network protocols, with practical work involving CISCO routers and switches.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in designing a hierarchical IPv4 addressing scheme. (D.1)
Design small to medium sized networks with switches and routers given design criteria. (C.1)
Build and operate network infrastructure services for small to medium sized networks. (D.1)
Demonstrate teamwork capability and communication skills. (E.1)
31277.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge in open system interconnection (OSI); transmission control protocol/internet protocol (TCP/IP) and data network models; knowledge of networking terminology, data transmission media, data networking components and devices; internet protocol addressing.

31282.title: Systems Testing and Quality Management
31282.description: This subject equips you with practical knowledge and skills for measuring and controlling software quality. You'll learn about software quality assurance, management principles, and testing approaches for systems and software.
learningOutcomes: Design specific processes, types and phases of testing to assure quality in software products (C.1)
Identify principles and approaches to testing and quality management to projects and business outcomes (D.1)
Apply a variety of testing techniques to evaluate system operations and functions (D.1)
Apply quality assurance and management principles in testing environment (D.1)
Collaboratively plan, develop, apply and document test quality systems (E.1)

31748.title: Programming on the Internet
31748.description: This subject equips you with an in-depth understanding of internet-based programming and the World Wide Web's intricacies, from its evolution to its technical core. You'll learn essential data presentation techniques and delve into the client/server model, focusing on website creation with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, MySQL/MongoDB, and modern JavaScript libraries for building user interfaces (e.g., React). The subject offers a solid foundation for grasping the WWW's workings, constructing websites, and mastering web software development through scripting.
learningOutcomes: Identify concepts pertaining to the Internet and World Wide web such as TCP/IP, protocols, domain names, IP addresses and n-tier architecture. (D.1)
Apply principles of internet security to websites. (D.1)
Apply principles of website design to improve efficiency using industry used web development languages. (D.1)
Apply client-side and server-side scripting to manage a range of simple web server interactions. (D.1)
Relate web development frameworks to effectively manage websites. (D.1)
31748.requisiteText: (1 AND (2 OR 2a OR 2b OR 2c OR 2d OR 2e))
31748.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have basic knowledge of programming languages (HTML, CSS, JavaScript)

31777.title: Advanced Interaction Design
31777.description: This subject focuses on user experience (UX) in interaction design, crucial for technology adoption and competitive edge. You'll learn conceptual tools to discuss, analyse, and critique UX with digital technologies. The subject covers a range of interactions like mobile, social, pervasive computing, and IoT, helping you understand how to design for specific user experiences in context. You'll also learn design methods like user research, sketching, prototyping, and evaluation to create technology solutions that are not only effective but engaging. By building on fundamental design concepts, you'll be equipped to design technologies that optimise user experience.
learningOutcomes: Use appropriate conceptual tools to accurately describe, critique, analyse and evaluate user experiences that arise through-and-during interactions with information technology. (D.1)
Identify the types of user experiences that are most appropriate for different types of human-computer interactions. (C.1)
Apply appropriate methods, concepts, and techniques to successfully design interactive technologies that can support engaging user experiences during use. (C.1)
Describe the range of social/technical and experiential concepts that are important to consider when designing technologies that can be experienced positively by users. (B.1)
Demonstrate awareness on how to design in a positive and respectful manner when working with, and for, Indigenous Australians. (A.1)
31777.recommended: It is recommended that students complete 48cp (2 years of full-time study) prior to commencing this subject.

31927.title: Application Development with .NET
31927.description: This subject introduces you to C# programming using Visual Studio and the .NET development framework. You will explore the .NET framework and its core concepts, applying this knowledge to develop applications in C#.
learningOutcomes: Understand the .NET framework architecture. (D.1)
Understand how the .NET framework implements OO concepts and the implications this has for new language design. (D.1)
Understand the mechanisms and techniques for the deployment and configuration of .NET applications. (D.1)
Be able to utilize the .NET libraries. (D.1)
Design and develop a C# program in the .NET environment. (C.1)
31927.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have a good understanding of programming constructs, O-O concepts and programming practices.

32009.title: Advanced Routing Principles
32009.description: This subject focuses on routing technology and provides a comprehensive explanation of routing. It extends your skills and knowledge in scalable interior and exterior routing protocols, policy-based routing, route optimisation and redistribution. Content is primarily drawn from CCNP Enterprise: Core Networking (ENCOR) with additional insights from CCNP Enterprise: Advanced Routing. The subject is run in the UTS Cisco Systems Network Academy.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate physical network infrastructure to recommend and operationalise appropriate for stakeholder needs. (B.1)
Compare and optimise interior and exterior scalable routing protocols in a multi-protocol scenario for internal connectivity and access to an Internet Service Provider (ISP). (D.1)
Explain the advantages and limitations of scalable routing protocols and their suitability for the small, medium and large enterprise. (D.1)

args.scope: spk(s): MAJ03445 - Networking and Cybersecurity major BSc

32011.title: Multilayer Switched Networks
32011.description: This subject advances your understanding and practical skills in designing and implementing switched campus networks, using VLANs to enhance performance, reliability, management, and security. You'll explore various approaches to plan, configure, and verify complex enterprise switching solutions, with hands-on experience on Cisco Systems layer 2 and layer 3 switches. The curriculum aligns with CCNP Enterprise: Core Networking (ENCOR) and is conducted at the UTS Cisco Systems Network Academy.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate the design benefits and limitations of switched campus networks by applying knowledge of the theoretical characteristics of different high-speed switched network technologies. (C.1)
Apply appropriate switched network technologies to meet needs of switched networks. (C.1)
Apply troubleshooting steps to solve problems encountered in switched LANs. (D.1)
Explain to technically informed people the merits of different modes of network configurations. (D.1)

args.scope: spk(s): MAJ03445 - Networking and Cybersecurity major BSc

32113.title: Advanced Database
32113.description: Software systems require trustworthy data management systems. This subject covers advanced database concepts, requirements, architecture, design and systems. Current trends and challenges in the practice of data management are explored to develop the robust data solutions. In small teams, students apply these contemporary data management practices to their advanced database project work. Students learn to integrate and manage data from different sources to support the data-intensive software systems.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate data design and management and its value in relation to supporting corporate stakeholder data resource. (B.1)
Design data models to support complex corporate stakeholder requirements. (C.1)
Create database systems and solutions to support a range of data types and structures to support complex queries and results. (D.1)
Collaborate effectively in a group to address a practical business problem. (E.1)

32130.title: Fundamentals of Data Analytics
32130.description: This subject equips you with both theoretical and hands-on experience of data analytics, the process of extracting meaningful insights from large data sets. You'll learn statistical methods and data visualisation techniques to explore and process vast volumes of data, and unsupervised as well as supervised techniques to discover patterns and insights for knowledge discovery. The subject synthesises cutting-edge research and practice, preparing you to lead data analytics projects that transform data into commercially valuable information.
learningOutcomes: Scope framed data informed business problems using contextual, ethical, and stakeholder awareness. (B.1)
Design data analytics approaches to business objectives and data constraints. (C.1)
Use appropriate data analytics methods to describe and implement descriptive and predictive analytics solutions. (D.1)
Communicate data analytics methods and insights effectively in oral and written forms, demonstrating responsible and critical collaboration with AI tools. (E.1)

32146.title: Data Visualisation and Visual Analytics
32146.description: This subject focuses on the vital technologies of data visualisation and visual interaction that underpin visual analytics and decision-making. You'll engage with recent data visualisation literature and practice using advanced software. The subject outlines the visual data analytics process and methodology, including the critical role of human interaction with interactive visual interfaces. Upon completion, you'll be adept at designing and evaluating sophisticated visualisation interfaces, positioning you for roles as a data visualisation designer and visual data analyst.
learningOutcomes: Recognise, compare and apply a range of static data visualisation techniques. (D.1)
Apply interactive data visualisation techniques. (D.1)
Design and create data visualisations for particular social contexts that are appropriate for specific users. (C.1)
Design and create data visualisations that facilitate the discovery and presentation of data-driven stories. (C.1)

32524.title: LANS and Routing
32524.description: This subject will provide you with a foundational understanding of how computer networks operate, particularly in the creation, operation, and maintenance of local area networks (LANs). You will develop a working knowledge of IP addressing schemes and essential routing and switching techniques within autonomous systems, using specialised networking devices to build small-to-medium networks. Utilising Cisco Networking Academy's online resources, you will engage in regular hands-on practice and gain real-world problem-solving skills by performing basic configuration and troubleshooting tasks with Cisco routers and switches.
learningOutcomes: Design small to medium-sized routed and switched networks, including hierarchical IP addressing schemes, to meet specified requirements. (C.1)
Apply computer network concepts and technologies to analyse and solve network problems. (D.1)
Utilise appropriate networking equipment and media to implement, troubleshoot and verify connectivity of small to medium-sized networks using Cisco hardware and software. (D.1)
Demonstrate teamwork skills in labs and projects to achieve specified requirements. (E.1)

32548.title: Cybersecurity
32548.description: This subject deepens your understanding of cybersecurity from both technical and management viewpoints. You'll explore and discuss cyber-attack methods and defense strategies using industry-standard tools. Key topics include cyber-attacks and defenses, web security, firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and security services like confidentiality, integrity, and authentication (CIA). You'll also learn about technologies including IPSec, SSL, PGP, and S/MIME. You will perform research on recent cyber-attacks and their mitigation methods to master the skills applied in industry context.
learningOutcomes: Recognise and compare major theories and principles that are used in the implementation of a secure network. (D.1)
Apply the underlying algorithms used to construct Security Protocols. (D.1)
Identify and recognise major security threats and their mitigation strategy. (D.1)
Explain the major methodologies for secure networks and what threat they address. (D.1)
32548.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have a good understanding of internet protocols, web systems and how interconnected systems are built using these protocols; a sound knowledge of using Unix/Linux system commands is required to complete lab exercises

32555.title: Fundamentals of Software Development
32555.description: This subject provides a foundation in modern software development, covering the theoretical and practical aspects of software modelling and development methods, tools, and techniques. You will learn how to analyse, design, develop, and evaluate software programs that implement realistic but manageably small-scale software requirements. Teaching is delivered through pre-recorded lectures and demos, hands-on workshops, and mini-lectures in these workshops. You are encouraged to practice peer learning and collaboration within and outside the classroom; however, you must complete the individual tasks and your part of the group tasks independently. By completing this subject, you will understand the importance of foundational software development practices and be able to apply programming skills to build software that meets the defined criteria.
learningOutcomes: Analyse and document system requirements based on user needs and context. (B.1)
Use a range of modelling and programming techniques and tools to propose software system for users. (C.1)
Design a software system to meet the specified user requirements. (C.1)
Create software programs to address the specified user requirements. (D.1)
Apply appropriate testing techniques to ensure the quality of the software system. (D.1)
