32606.title: Database
32606.description: This subject introduces basic concepts of database design and its implementation, including relational design through entity-relationship diagrams and their interpretation. You'll learn to use SQL for data retrieval from databases and gain skills into the coding required for database implementation.
learningOutcomes: Design an Entity-Relationship (E-R) model from specifications and transform a conceptual model into corresponding logical data structures. (C.1)
Construct Structured Query Language (SQL) statements and maintain a simple database. (D.1)
Critically evaluate database designs and the role databases play in effective software applications. (C.1)
Effectively communicate database design. (E.1)
32606.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject are familiar with basic system analysis concepts and have basic software skills.

33116.title: Design, Data, and Decisions
33116.description: This subject focuses on data analysis. You will learn how to collect and analyse data, and how to draw valid conclusions from the data. You'll begin by examining how to sample from a population, and how to describe the data collected. You will then explore how to form and test hypotheses about the population using the data collected from the sample.
learningOutcomes: select and produce appropriate graphical, tabular and numerical summaries of variables in a data set, and summarise such information
distinguish between observational and experimental studies, and draw conclusions appropriate to each type of study
determine whether an interval or a test is more appropriate for addressing a particular question, and apply these concepts to answer questions using real data involving a single variable
choose the appropriate type of inference to answer questions using real data involving several variables
analyse, assess and critique statistical arguments of the type found in the popular press and in scholarly publications

33130.title: Mathematics 1
33130.description: This subject helps you develop the knowledge and skills necessary for problem-solving and mathematical modelling at an introductory level. You will apply differential calculus to model situations in science and engineering that involve oscillations. Integral calculus is used to solve selected problems involving first- and second-order differential equations, and to calculate areas, volumes, lengths and other physical quantities. You will be introduced to vectors, matrix multiplication and determinants, and apply them to problem-solving and modelling. You'll also review sequences and series and be introduced to power series to approximate more functions.
learningOutcomes: Describe the relevance of mathematics to engineering and science and the role which engineering and science play in the development and evolution of mathematical ideas and methods.
Apply mathematical tools and resources to model real world problems in engineering and science.
Demonstrate correct use of mathematical terminology and concepts, and show understanding of those concepts by describing them in both formal and informal language.
Achieve a high level of skill in the mathematical techniques covered in the subject content.
Communicate mathematical knowledge clearly, logically and critically.

args.text: Must be admitted to course C00001-C10445
Must be admitted to course C10448-C10479
Must be admitted to course C10481-C99999

33130.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed HSC Extension 1 Mathematics.

33230.title: Mathematics 2
33230.description: This subject is split into multivariate calculus and introductory statistics. You'll develop mathematical skills for modelling systems with multiple variables and learn descriptive statistics, statistical inference, and simple linear regression. Key topics include linear algebra, solving equation sets, eigenvectors and eigenvalues, partial derivatives, optimisation, multiple integrals, probability, particularly in assessing component reliability in engineering.
learningOutcomes: Apply and justify mathematical and statistical tools and techniques to model and solve real-world engineering.
Communicate complex mathematical and statistical concepts clearly and logically using both formal and informal language.
Demonstrate a high level of skill in the mathematical and statistical techniques covered in the subject by both formulating and solving problems in engineering and science.
Demonstrate understanding of the theoretical results which justify the use of these techniques.
Use appropriate software tools to perform calculations and explore ideas.

35007.title: Mathematics 3
35007.description: This subject develops advanced methods in vector calculus, partial differential equations, and complex analysis. It covers vector fields and differential operators, including the Laplacian, and introduces techniques such as Fourier series and Green’s functions for solving differential equations. The subject also studies analytic functions, contour integration, and residue calculus. Applications are drawn from differential equations, signal analysis, and mathematical modelling.
learningOutcomes: Apply techniques from vector calculus, including differentiation and integration of scalar and vector fields, to solve problems in physical and mathematical contexts.
Analyse and solve partial differential equations using methods such as separation of variables and Fourier series.
Demonstrate understanding of complex functions, including differentiation, integration, and series expansions in the complex plane.
Apply contour integration and residue theory to evaluate integrals and solve applied problems.
Communicate mathematical reasoning and solutions clearly, and interpret results in the context of mathematical modelling applications.

35010.title: Foundation Mathematics
35010.description: Quantitative knowledge and skills are fundamental to many disciplines and many professions. This subject aims to provide students with opportunities to acquire essential knowledge and skills in fundamental quantitative areas including basic algebra, functions and calculus. This subject aims to increase students' confidence in the basic mathematics topics to ensure smooth and confident transition to further quantitative subjects in their chosen area of study. This subject is core to transition from school forming the 'Pathway', which is a program of support, in place, to help if you do not have calculus training.
learningOutcomes: apply fundamental concepts of mathematics to solve problems in their chosen area of study
use mathematical, engineering and scientific terminology and symbols to define concepts
recognise different representations of the same concept, such as algebraic and graphical
apply mathematical knowledge and skills in a variety of situations, in both familiar and new contexts

36103.title: Statistical Thinking for Data Science
36103.description: This subject instills the statistical thinking central to data science, teaching you to apply statistical methods to extract insights from data. You'll start with fundamental principles and modern inference methods, gaining hands-on experience with real-world data. Progressing to statistical models and estimation techniques, you'll complete a data science research cycle, formulating questions, analyzing data, and communicating results effectively. The subject begins with workshops and lectures, transitioning to self-directed learning, fostering your growth as a data scientist. By the end, you'll have a solid foundation in the technical, conceptual, and practical realms of data science.
learningOutcomes: Manage data science project complexities.
Formulate precise data science inquiries and justify the use of appropriate statistical concepts and tools to respond to those questions.
Find, clean, and merge datasets from a range of sources to answer real world data science problems.
Apply appropriate statistical methods for datasets and interpret and communicate the results in ways that suit the needs of diverse stakeholders.
Engage with the local and global data science professional community to build ethical practices and responsibilities when working with Indigenous data and communities.

36106.title: Machine Learning Algorithms and Applications
36106.description: This subject introduces students to key machine learning algorithms and their application in real-world settings. Participants are guided in developing an intuitive understanding of how the algorithms work, as well as their strengths and weaknesses. In addition to gaining practical experience with the algorithms, students develop an understanding of the basic principles of machine learning and the connections between different algorithms. Additionally, they are exposed to industry standard methodologies for data mining and analytics via readings and assessments. Since data science problems are infused with assumptions, often with ethical and legal implications, due attention is given to questioning the assumptions behind data and approaches used to analyse it.
learningOutcomes: Apply an industry standard analytics life cycle methodology for data mining and pattern discovery
Interpret, synthesise and communicate insights extracted from machine learning algorithms in a context-appropriate manner.
Articulate the strengths, weaknesses and assumptions of a selection of machine learning algorithms in relation to structured and unstructured data
Execute and interpret machine learning approaches available for extracting value from data
Demonstrate an appreciation, with examples, of a critical, ethical perspective on decisions made throughout the analytics lifecycle

37161.title: Probability and Random Variables
37161.description: This subject equips you with probability concepts to quantify and model uncertainty in real-world scenarios. You'll learn about dependent and independent events, conditional probability, and modelling random events using distributions. Key topics include probability calculation, expectation, variance, generating functions, and order statistics for independent events, culminating in an exploration of discrete Markov chains.
learningOutcomes: understand, explain and prove the principal ideas and results concerning the study of probability and random variables.
apply the concepts of probability and random variables to simple problems, using computational skills where appropriate.
extract key information from a text and interpret this in correct mathematical terminology.
Use an appropriate combination of formulae and prose to explain a solution to a problem

37181.title: Discrete Mathematics
37181.description: This subject lays the groundwork for logical reasoning and methodology, crucial for computer science and mathematics students. You’ll tackle the fundamentals of logic, proof techniques, set theory, functions, counting, complexity and correctness of algorithms, and elementary number theory with applications to cryptography.
learningOutcomes: Solve simple problems in discrete mathematics and apply this knowledge to solve selected problems arising in other parts of science, in engineering and business
Understand and apply knowledge of discrete mathematics and its theoretical underpinnings by constructing logical, clearly presented and justified arguments incorporating deductive reasoning
Identify where the basic concepts of discrete mathematics are useful in addressing a real world problem

Engage in group discussions to decide upon the appropriate choice of techniques from discrete mathematics to describe a wide variety of problems from fields including the physical sciences, engineering and business

37233.title: Linear Algebra
37233.description: This subject provides students with a grasp of linear algebra and its most fundamental aspects. It covers systems of linear equations, vector spaces and subspaces, basis, coordinates, linear transformations, eigenvectors and eigenvalues, scalar products, orthogonality, projections, diagonalisation and singular value decomposition.
learningOutcomes: Apply appropriate linear algebra techniques to solve mathematical problems.
Implement suitable algorithms in linear algebra.
Collaborate effectively in group discussions.
Communicate concepts and results of linear algebra using rigorous mathematical proofs, and prepare for practical applications.

37242.title: Introduction to Optimisation
37242.description: This subject introduces the optimization methods and quantitative management concepts that are essential for decision-making in the fields such as supply chain management, financial analysis, transportation, production planning, and scheduling. The subject focuses on optimization techniques for linear programming models,and introduces basic nonlinear optimization and integer programming concepts and methods, and their applications.
learningOutcomes: Apply fundamental principles and concepts of mathematical programming to analyse tractable simplifications of real-world problems in quantitative management and engineering, and demonstrate the understanding of the limitations of the simplified problem formulations;
Choose and implement the most appropriate mathematical programming method to solve a particular optimisation problem
Present the results of modelling task in a written report providing concise mathematical programming-based analysis and explanation of the methodology used.

Reflect on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples’ unique connection to Country and knowledge systems to inform inclusive, ethical mathematical and statistical modelling with and for Indigenous Australians

37252.title: Regression and Linear Models
37252.description: This subject teaches regression analysis, a method for modelling relationships between a response variable and multiple explanatory variables. Regression analysis is widely used in fields such as science, engineering, medicine, and business. The subject covers the development and testing of multivariable models and techniques for deciding which set of variables gives the best model.
learningOutcomes: Formulate and solve problems by applying appropriate regression analysis models and techniques.
Use the statistical package (R) to conduct regression analysis and interpret the results of the analysis.
Communicate clearly the results of a statistical analysis.
Develop teamwork and professional collaboration skills.
Independently source a suitable data set and apply simple linear regression techniques to the data set.

37262.title: Mathematical Statistics
37262.description: This subject extends your skills in probability theory and its relation to statistical methods. You will see how to quantify uncertainties in real-world scenarios, including problems with more than one variable. The topics you will see include goodness-of-fit tests, regression models and the mathematical underpinnings of these concepts alongside their practical application. Additionally, you will be introduced to Bayesian statistics as well as contemporary computational procedures for Bayesian statistics, including Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods.
learningOutcomes: Explain and prove the principal ideas and results underpinning the fields of probability and statistics.
Select and apply statistical techniques to a variety of datasets to evaluate hypotheses.
Interpret and clearly communicate the results of appropriate statistical tests in everyday language.
Apply critical and creative thinking to address complex problems selecting suitable models and techniques.

37345.title: Quantitative Management Practice
37345.description: This subject addresses the practical aspects of quantitative management and recent advancements in areas such as personnel scheduling, supply chain management, production planning, transportation, and finance. It includes case studies and analysis of recent journal publications, aiming to develop professional skills and apply knowledge gained from other quantitative management studies.
learningOutcomes: Implement advanced techniques to solve a range of quantitative management problems using industry standard software.
Assess the mathematical aspects of an industrial application and the appropriateness of different mathematical/statistical approaches to its solution.
Develop high quality written and oral presentations, with depth and comprehensiveness appropriate to a range of stakeholders involved in industry-based management.
Identify different approaches to solving a range of complex quantitative management problems within their industrial contexts.
Understand and apply knowledge needed to solve a complex quantitative management problem, and critically review approaches that other people have taken to solving the problem.

37363.title: Stochastic Processes and Financial Mathematics
37363.description: This subject introduces the mathematics of random processes, essential for describing and predicting complex system behaviours relevant to disciplines from finance to physics. It covers Gaussian-Markov processes, Brownian motion, Markov chains, birth-death processes, Compound Poisson processes, time series, diffusion processes and Ito’s Lemma, and financial modelling including the Black-Scholes formula.
learningOutcomes: Define key concepts and demonstrate techniques of proof used in probability and stochastic processes.
Apply fundamental theorems to solve problems in probability.
Use mathematical techniques to analyse the behaviour of various stochastic processes.
Formulate and solve applied and theoretical problems involving probability and stochastic processes.
Communicate effectively about probability and stochastic processes.

37495.title: Statistical Design and Models for Evaluation Studies
37495.description: This subject explores evaluation study methods, advancing from regression models to include basic randomised control trials (RCTs), survey design and estimation, time series analysis for interventions like the Sydney 'Lock-Out Laws', propensity score adjustment, and two-stage regression. Real-world case studies exemplify these techniques. Additionally, it examines statistical design concepts concerning internal versus external validity.
learningOutcomes: Present clear and persuasive arguments to diverse audiences.
Design and implement experiments appropriate to various contexts in industry and public policy.
Implement advanced techniques to solve authentic problems using industry standard software.
Propose solutions to mitigate ethical issues when designing a study or presenting analysis.
Produce a comprehensive report summarising a substantial research project.

40005.title: Advanced iOS Development
40005.description: This subject offers an advanced insight into iOS application development with Swift and SwiftUI, where you'll master complex concepts, frameworks, and tools to create robust, innovative iOS apps. It emphasises hands-on experience with industry-standard practices, pushing you to devise solutions that address real-world software needs.
learningOutcomes: Design well-structured solution blueprints that satisfy given software requirements within the iOS development environment. (C.1)
Develop skills and competencies in implementing a solution using Swift programming language with the iOS development environment. (D.1)
Work with teams when designing and developing iOS applications and communicate the developed solution to a wider audience. (E.1)

40006.title: iOS industry Studio
40006.description: This studio is designed to enhance your practical iOS application development skills to become professionally competent. You will participate in reflective design practices, collaborate in teams, receive mentorship and learn advanced techniques. This hands-on learning experience will provide you with a comprehensive understanding of the iOS development environment and its frameworks to deliver real-world applications.
learningOutcomes: Identify the social impacts of iOS applications. (B.1)
Design a solution to demonstrate software skills with SwiftUI. (C.1)
Demonstrate technical capability in software development techniques and tools with SwiftUI. (D.1)
Demonstrate communication and collaboration skills in a team to develop iOS applications. (E.1)
Critically self-review their performance to improve themselves and their teams. (F.1)

40007.title: iOS Innovation Studio
40007.description: This Foundational studio subject offers you a challenge-based learning environment where you will develop fundamental skills in solving real-world problems, collaborating in diverse teams, and designing and developing apps within the Apple iOS ecosystem. The subject empowers you with a skill set at the intersection of technology, creativity, and entrepreneurship. Through the studio experience, you will work in multidisciplinary cohorts mixing with peers from a range of backgrounds and experiences to work through the design thinking process to develop a semi-functional iOS prototype app.
learningOutcomes: Identify and engage with a range of project stakeholders to obtain domain-specific knowledge. (B.1)
Apply Design Thinking approaches to design user-friendly digital solutions to meet stakeholder requirements. (C.1)
Produce a semi-functional prototype using Swift and Xcode to implement an iOS app. (D.1)
Collaboratively articulate project milestones based on feedback and teamwork that address a real-world problem. (E.1)
Reflect throughout design and development process with feedback to justify areas of, and potential for, professional growth as IOS technologist. (F.1)

41001.title: Cloud Computing and Software as a Service
41001.description: This subject introduces you to cloud computing, covering cloud architecture, IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, virtualisation, and multi-tenancy. You'll engage in group work to produce a research report critically analysing a cloud computing aspect, followed by developing cloud-based software engineering skills on an existing platform. The second assignment involves group collaboration to create a cloud-based software application.
learningOutcomes: Articulate the need for cloud computing, elements of cloud computing for e-business, e-government, e-banking, e-health and e-learning. (B.1)
Describe the architecture of different types of Cloud Services (IaaS, PaaS and SaaS), different types of Virtualization and their industrial use. (D.1)
Critically understand the current issues in Cloud Computing for informed business decision making. (D.1)
Create a Cloud Computing prototye that will be on a Cloud platform for areas such as e-government, e-banking, e-health and e-learning. (C.1)

41012.title: Programming for Mechatronic Systems
41012.description: This subject lays out the theoretical foundations of object-oriented programming using C++, honing your skills in designing, implementing and managing code for moderately complex mechatronics systems. You'll learn to create modular, reusable, reliable, and maintainable code. Through an individual project, you'll apply these concepts to design and implement components of a mechatronic system, tackling real-life challenges. The curriculum covers objects, classes, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, threading, event handling, and the use of C++ standard features like the STL, APIs, middleware, as well as documentation and testing strategies.
learningOutcomes: Design classes that are reusable, reliable and maintainable. (C.1)
Apply theoretical knowledge of sensors and control to practical programming problems. (D.1)
Select appropriate class structures and data handling methods for task at hand. (D.1)
Implement and test object-oriented applications of moderate complexity. (D.1)
Communicate programming design decisions, dependencies, interconnections, use cases and testing procedures in a written document. (E.1)
41012.requisiteText: ((1) OR (2 AND (3 OR 3a OR 3b OR 3c OR 3d)))
41012.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of the C language and digital systems

41019.title: Prototyping Physical Interaction
41019.description: This subject hones your ability to design, assess, and implement interactive physical devices with a human-centred approach. You'll learn to prototype using sensors, actuators, and diverse display methods to enhance user interaction and experience. By processing sensor data and designing multimodal feedback, you'll refine your prototypes through iterative user assessments, progressively perfecting the design.
learningOutcomes: Use a human-centred design process to design and develop an interactive system. (C.1)
Model a physical interactive system for a project. (C.1)
Embed sensors and process sensor data to support the user experience of a physical interactive system. (D.1)
Assess the usability and appropriateness of an interactive system through studying use in context. (C.1)
Communicate design and implementation strategies effectively to a range of disciplinary and non-disciplinary stakeholders. (E.1)
41019.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have some basic programming knowledge, but no particular language knowledge is assumed.

41020.title: Human-centred Design Methods
41020.description: This subject focuses on making people the core of the interaction design process through human-centred design methods, with particular attention to the interviewing and probes methods. Interviewing gathers direct information and adapts flexibly across the design process, while probes, using tailored props, require more setup but aim to inspire creative insights and prepare participants for a follow-up interview. You'll learn both methods, applying them step-by-step to real participants, guided by a brief and with readings and examples to tailor your approach. You must recruit at least three strangers (people you do not know and who are not familiar with the subject) for interviews and one stranger for the probe study.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of human-centred design methods. (D.1)
Demonstrate an ability to plan, design and carry out small user research projects. (C.1)
Develop an analysis of the findings from user research suitable for use in professional projects. (B.1)
Explain results and outcomes to others in their cohort and to broader audiences through paper writing, poster and video presentations. (E.1)
Apply positive and respectful ethical practices, such as the AIATSIS Code and NHMRC’s ethical code for researchers. (A.1, B.1)
41020.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject be familiar with the basics of human-computer interaction, human-centred design and evaluation methods; the principles and use of iterative design cycles of reflection, prototype (re)design and evaluation; and issues relating to data gathering and analysis.

41025.title: Introduction to Software Development
41025.description: This subject introduces the fundamentals of modern software development, more specifically, website development. You will learn traditional and agile software development principles, methods, tools, and techniques, and explore current trends and challenges in software development. You will also learn how to design, develop, and evaluate software that implements commercially realistic but manageably small requirements. Teaching is delivered through pre-recorded lectures and hands-on workshops. In your weekly workshops and assessment tasks, you will be given assignments to modify or extend existing software features or functions and, at times, to create new ones. You will be encouraged to practice peer learning and collaboration, but ultimately, you must complete your tasks independently. By successfully completing this subject, you will experience, understand the importance of, and be able to apply sound professional practices in software development.
learningOutcomes: Investigate and solve software development problems with minimal supervision. (C.1)
Determine and balance the competing goals of software development activities within their constraints. (C.1)
Plan and manage a software development task to create, modify or extend a software feature or function to completion within the task constraints. (C.1)
Apply sound software engineering practices to successfully create, modify or extend a software feature or function. (C.1)
Communicate clearly software and task information to interested stakeholders. (E.1)

41026.title: Advanced Software Development
41026.description: This subject advances your understanding of software development, such as the design, development, and evaluation of a complex software system that fulfills specific functional and non-functional requirements. You will work in highly autonomous teams that, while supervised and directed, take full responsibility for the project and delivery of the expected outcomes. The subject focuses on professional practices including team management, project planning, and all key software development processes. You will also make and justify informed design decisions, enhancing your capability to deliver sound software solutions.
learningOutcomes: Elicit and manage customer requirements throughout the project. (B.1)
Design, construct and evaluate software to meet customer requirements. (C.1)
Implement a complex software development project using optimal methods and designs. (D.1)
Collaborate with team in a range of roles to manage the software development project to completion. (E.1)
Communicate relevant and timely project, software and team information to all stakeholders. (E.1)
41026.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have competence in programming and software development methods and tools

41039.title: Programming 1
41039.description: This subject provides a foundation in core programming concepts, vital for careers in computer science and software development. It emphasises project-based learning, independent research, and effective communication. You'll also be introduced to real-world programming practices, preparing you to tackle complex industry-level projects. This approach ensures you develop the multifaceted skill set required for solving sophisticated programming challenges.
learningOutcomes: Apply basic programming concepts of state, iteration, and decision. (D.1)
Solve computational problems by using abstract modelling and conceptualisation. (D.1)
Design and create simple functioning programs to achieve objectives. (C.1)
Interpret, describe, and document programs using clear communication. (E.1)
Reflect on programming decisions and formulate alternatives. (C.1)

41040.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
41040.description: This subject enhances your grasp of Artificial Intelligence (AI), covering learning, natural language processing, computer vision, search, knowledge representation, and reasoning. With lectures and practical labs focused on specific AI techniques, you'll learn to select appropriate models and algorithms for tasks and apply AI methods in simple applications. You will be assessed by a knowledge test, a set of mini-AI application examples and a group project addressing a real-world problem using AI technique, reflecting your ability for exemplifying AI applications and designing AI solutions in practical scenarios.
learningOutcomes: Explain key concepts and applications of AI techniques. (D.1)
Design solutions to implement AI techniques to solve simple real world problems. (C.1)
Communicate the application of AI techniques in collaboration with team members. (E.1)
41040.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed 33230 Mathematics 2 and 37181 Discrete Mathematics. It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have epxerience with linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete logic

41052.title: Advanced Algorithms
41052.description: Algorithms are the heart of computer science and information technology. This subject dives deeply into more advanced data structures and algorithmic techniques for solving problems, particularly graph and optimisation problems. You will practice implementing these ideas to solve new problems, gain experience testing and evaluating the performance of algorithms, and learn to communicate algorithmic strategies effectively.
learningOutcomes: Understand computational problems and consider possible solutions in the context of their application areas. (D.1)
Apply advanced data structures, programming techniques and algorithmic paradigms to create efficient algorithms for computational problems. (C.1)
Evaluate the computational complexity of a problem or algorithm. (D.1)
Communicate the functioning of complex algorithms in collaboration with peers. (E.1)

41076.title: Methods in Quantum Computing
41076.description: This subject offers a structured introduction to quantum computing, a revolutionary technology poised to surpass traditional computing capabilities. You'll learn the fundamental principles, discover quantum algorithms, and acquire programming skills to develop software that leverages the extraordinary potential of quantum computers, preparing you for advancements expected in the near future.
learningOutcomes: Explain the advantages of quantum computing over classical computing. (D.1)
Evaluate the application of quantum computing technologies to known and unknown contexts. (D.1)
Analyse efficiency and complexity of quantum technologies. (D.1)

41078.title: Computing Science Studio 1
41078.description: This subject immerses you in the world of computer science research, examining its purpose and methodologies. You will develop academic writing skills for literature reviews and reports, explore research collaboration, leadership, and ethics, and under mentor guidance, investigate chosen topics. There's encouragement to consult with leading computer scientists and a focus on honing communication, ethical, and analytical skills vital for a career in computing science.
learningOutcomes: Identify the social and ethical impacts of computer science research in a given context. (B.1)
Design a methodological solution to systematically review a research field/topic. (C.1)
Implement a set of analytical methods, tools, and strategies to analyse and evaluate academic resources. (D.1)
Construct written, spoken, and visual communication with teamwork. (E.1)
Reflect self-development, learning experience, and collaborative interactions. (F.1)

requisite.scope: spk(s): C09119 - Bachelor of Computing Science (Honours)

41078.recommended: It is recommended that students complete all 1st-year Bachelor of Computing Science (Honours) subjects prior to commencing this subject.

41080.title: Theory of Computing Science
41080.description: This subject explores the theory of computation, covering automata, decidability, and computational complexity. These topics provide key tools for you to perform rewriting and parsing, and to determine the complexity of various problems. Understanding computational complexity is crucial for creating cost-effective and practical solutions, such as optimising large-scale problems in online services. Additionally, a firm grasp of computational theory underpins the creation of user-friendly, secure systems and the identification of performance issues in programming, leading to more efficient algorithm design.
learningOutcomes: Build models for real-world applications and plan computations realisable on computers. (C.1)
Formulate the Turing machine computation model using formal definition and higher-level operation description. (D.1)
Distinguish some decidable/non-decidable problems by proof in the Turing machine computation framework. (D.1)
Analyse algorithm efficiency and improve when possible. (D.1)

41082.title: Introduction to Data Engineering
41082.description: This subject lays the groundwork for understanding data engineering and its role in today's data-driven world. You'll actively engage in designing data collection experiments, processing and analysing data, and visualising it effectively for informed decision-making. You'll gather your own datasets or work with existing datasets for class activities and a culminating project. Proficiency in MATLAB, essential for modelling and analysis, is a key outcome. The subject is a core component for Data Science Engineering majors but is also open to students from other disciplines seeking to enhance their data engineering skills.
learningOutcomes: Use practical skills to model and simulate complex and complicated systems. (D.1)
Understand, collect and store data. (D.1)
Validate, visualise and authenticate data. (D.1)
Characterise the role of data engineering in data science projects. (B.1)
Design, perform and evaluate a data gathering activity using the Matlab environment. (C.1)

41084.title: Fundamentals Studio A
41084.description: This studio, the first in the fundamentals stage for Data and Electronic Engineering majors, moves beyond traditional curricula to foster an environment where you can apply and expand your knowledge through practical experience. It's centred on product development, requiring collaborative work in the studio with peers, academics, and industry mentors. You'll undertake a mix of self-directed study and team-based project work, progressing through stages of assessment, design, and implementation, mirroring the classic engineering process. Guided by a learning contract set at the start, you'll focus on acquiring fundamental skills and knowledge to realise basic product functionality, with an emphasis on creativity, technical expertise, teamwork, communication, and project management. Utilise this opportunity to delve into new topics that complement your coursework and personal interests.
learningOutcomes: Identify needs of a product owner and formulate product requirements to address those needs. (B.1)
Model, prototype and/or build a product to meet requirements. (C.1)
Demonstrate advancement of fundamental knowledge and skills appropriate to the student's discipline. (D.1)
Collaboratively work in defined roles to solve complex problems (E.1)
Demonstrate personal reflection on learning through engineering record keeping and knowledge sharing with peers (F.1)

41085.title: Fundamentals Studio B
41085.description: In this second studio of the Data and Electronic Engineering fundamentals stage, you're not confined to a standard curriculum but given the freedom to apply and enhance your knowledge through doing. The studio is a dynamic workspace where you'll collaborate with peers, academics, and industry mentors on product-based projects, blending individual study with team effort. Through the engineering process—assess, design, implement—you learn to apply knowledge to practical achievements. A learning contract directs your individual tasks from the outset. Here, you'll build on fundamental knowledge and skills to create a functioning product, emphasising creativity, diverse methods, technical growth, teamwork, communication, and project management. This studio is your chance to broaden your understanding by integrating new, personally interesting topics with previous coursework.
learningOutcomes: Identify needs of a product owner and formulate product requirements to address those needs. (B.1)
Model, prototype and/or build a product to meet requirements. (C.1)
Demonstrate advancement of fundamental knowledge and skills appropriate to the student's discipline. (D.1)
Collaboratively work in defined roles to solve complex problems (E.1)
Demonstrate personal reflection on learning through engineering record keeping and knowledge sharing with peers (F.1).

41091.title: Data Systems
41091.description: This subject delves into systems engineering for complex, data-centric systems, covering their lifecycle from design to management. You'll learn to build data pipelines through Extract, Transform, Load processes, apply Python for data engineering and reporting, and explore the Hadoop ecosystem and cloud data system providers. The learning experience is project-based, combining workshops on data engineering with collaborative project work, equipping you with practical, in-demand skills.
learningOutcomes: Define requirements and specifications of data system. (B.1)
Demonstrate a systematic design and thinking process for data system development. (C.1)
Prototype or implement data system according to system specifications. (D.1)
Communicate effectively to data system project stakeholders. (E.1)
Work effectively in a team to develop a data system, demonstrating continuous improvement and independence. (E.1, F.1)

41092.title: Network Fundamentals
41092.description:
This subject introduces the principles and practice of modern computer networking through a top-down exploration of the Internet and the TCP/IP protocol suite. Using Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach as the core text, students examine how networked applications communicate, how data is transported reliably and efficiently, how packets are routed across networks, and how link-layer technologies support end-to-end communication.

The subject combines conceptual understanding with practical experience. Students will analyse live network traffic, develop client-server applications using socket programming, and configure Cisco networking equipment to design and build functional networks. Through these activities, students will strengthen their ability to troubleshoot network behaviour, evaluate network services, and design efficient, reliable applications and network solutions.

By the end of the subject, students will have a solid foundation in Internet architecture, network protocols, and practical networking skills relevant to IT, software, data engineering, and cloud-connected systems.
learningOutcomes: Understand the key architectural principles of the Internet, namely protocol layering and service models. (D.1)
Analyse various components of the Internet, including Applications, Transport, Network, Addressing, and Data Link, to select the most appropriate network services. (C.1)
Examine and explain end-to-end packet delivery throughout the network system to gain insight into the behaviour of the Internet. (D.1)
Design and implement network applications to provide a service, such as web and email. (C.1)
41092.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have basic programming skills, such as Python, in order to complete the programming projects

41113.title: Software Development Studio
41113.description: This studio subject focuses on the practical aspects of software development, fostering a rich and engaging practice-based environment to enhance your professional competence. It emphasises reflective design, teamwork, mentoring, and learning through tackling challenging problems. You will form teams with your peers to simulate a real software development team, interacting with industry or academic clients to understand their requirements and deliver software solutions. Teaching is delivered through mini-lectures in studio sessions, covering topics such as version control and agile project management. In the assessments, you will demonstrate your software design and development skills, as well as your skill in reflective practice. By completing this subject, you will be equipped with knowledge and experience that is in high demand in industry.
learningOutcomes: Develop communication and collaboration skills in a team. (E.1)
Build capability in reflective practice. (F.1)
Build capability in software design skills. (C.1)
Build technical capability in software development techniques and tools. (D.1)

41174.title: Quantum Algorithms
41174.description: You'll gain proficiency in fundamental quantum algorithms, such as Shor's algorithm for integer factorisation and Grover's search algorithm. From there, you’ll learn about quantum walks, simulation of quantum systems, and algorithms for solving linear equations.
learningOutcomes: Write algorithms in the quantum circuit model. (D.1)
Apply the quantum algorithms learned to new problems and describe solutions. (C.1)
Demonstrate and communicate limitations of quantum algorithms. (E.1)

41180.title: Data Analytics in Cybersecurity
41180.description: Data Analytics for Cybersecurity equips you with the skills to leverage big data and threat intelligence in combating both insider and external cyber threats. You will learn to apply statistical methods to discern patterns and use intelligent technologies to identify security issues from data. The subject introduces machine learning applications in cybersecurity and standard data analytics processes. Through hands-on exercises, you will develop practical skills in analysing corporate computer and network vulnerabilities, thereby enhancing your ability to identify and mitigate security risks. This subject bridges the gap between data analytics and cybersecurity, providing you with the tools to effectively protect modern digital infrastructures.
learningOutcomes: Apply data analytics to investigate cybersecurity datasets. (D.1)
Detect and analyse cyber‐attacks using data analytics. (D.1)
Synthesise data analytics with other techniques to appropriately set rules for intrusion detection. (D.1)
Clearly communicate process of data analysis and security recommendations to a broad audience. (E.1)

41181.title: Information Security and Management
41181.description: This subject focuses on training you in IT security policy development and human security management while addressing critical legal and ethical considerations. You will lay the groundwork for applying cyber safety and security measures at a corporate level. By conducting security assessments within business constraints, you will learn to employ professional methodologies effectively. The subject also covers the systematic evaluation of business and security operations, equipping you with skills in contingency planning, risk assessment, risk management, and compliance across diverse business environments. You'll be prepared to develop comprehensive security policies and manage human factors in cybersecurity, ensuring robust protection and ethical governance within organisations.
learningOutcomes: Investigate security management issues in organisations by analysing requirements, plans and IT security policies. (B.1)
Propose appropriate information security protection mechanisms by assessing security risks, threats and vulnerabilities. (B.1)
Identify security training and education needs and associated legal and ethical awareness for organisational personnel. (B.1)
Apply organisational planning and project management principles to IT security planning individually and collaboratively. (E.1)
Demonstrate awareness on how to assess and identify cyber security issues when working with, and for, Indigenous Australians. (A.1)
41181.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b OR 1c OR 1d OR 1e OR 1f) AND (2 OR 2a OR 2b OR 2c))

41182.title: System Security
41182.description: This subject provides a comprehensive understanding of contemporary system security concepts, strategies, and practical techniques essential for securing operating systems, databases, and servers. You will learn to implement security measures throughout the design and configuration phases, ensuring robust system security and privacy. The subject places a strong emphasis on system hardening mechanisms and prominent security techniques, which you will apply in hands-on practical sessions. By testing the resilience of hardened systems against various attack vectors, you will gain critical skills in defending against real-world cybersecurity threats. This subject fosters both theoretical knowledge and practical expertise, preparing you to effectively safeguard corporate computing environments.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain the difference between particular types of security systems. (D.1)
Identify and analyse security vulnerabilities and issues in computer systems. (D.1)
Propose and justify technical solutions and potential remedy actions to increase security. (D.1)
Communicate with peers effectively concerning ethical hacking practice. (E.1)
41182.requisiteText: ((1 OR 1a OR 1b OR 1c OR 1d OR 1e OR 1f OR 1g OR 1h OR 1i))

41183.title: Privacy Preserving
41183.description: In this subject you'll master techniques for safeguarding data privacy, enabling organisations to handle personal or confidential data responsibly. The subject explores privacy models to build defenses against privacy breaches, delving into data anonymisation, statistical privacy approaches, and differential privacy, ensuring you can protect and manage sensitive information effectively.
learningOutcomes: Identify and explain the most common privacy models that are used in various communities and organisations. (B.1)
Evaluate the effectiveness of existing privacy measures. (D.1)
Apply privacy preserving techniques appropriate to a variety of security configurations and scenarios. (D.1)
Work as a team to investigate a real‐world privacy breach in a corporate environment. (E.1)

41184.title: Secure Programming and Penetration Testing
41184.description: This subject will equip you with the knowledge and skills necessary to develop secure software and assess the security of systems through source code analysis and penetration testing techniques. There will be coverage of the principles and practices of secure coding, the identification and mitigation of vulnerabilities, software verification, and the methodologies used in penetration testing. You will learn how to approach and develop automatic auditing systems, identifying vulnerabilities and developing security analysis and testing methods to protect systems against cyber-attacks. Additionally, you'll have the chance to engage in national and international security challenges, with assessments on secure programming, software analysis, and your communication skills in speaking and writing.
learningOutcomes: Classify software security vulnerabilities in the source code of systems, applications, and services. (D.1)
Automate the analysis of a software project using source code analysis on top of compilers to defend against real‐world attacks from malicious entities. (D.1)
Communicate effectively individually and as a team to describe plans for countering changing security threats. (E.1)
41184.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge experience with C/C++; Code Analysis; Compilers.

41185.title: Emerging Topics in Cybersecurity and Privacy
41185.description: This subject delves into contemporary IT security theories and practical skills in the cybersecurity profession, enhanced by guest lectures and workshops. You will develop a professional understanding of cybersecurity by examining emerging threats to web applications and systems, along with cutting-edge privacy and ethical issues. You'll explore current trends and challenges through professional practice and literature review. Working in small teams, you'll apply modern techniques for requirements elicitation, analysis, modelling, specification, and validation to real-world projects.
learningOutcomes: Examine various aspects of security systems according to new research outcomes and evolving understandings of security threats. (D.1)
Evaluate the design, implementation, configuration and application of existing security systems based on the latest IT security research outcomes. (C.1)
Synthesize literature and practically apply new research outcomes and approaches to real problems. (C.1)
Collaborate to communicate research synthesis alongside practical results. (E.1)

41191.title: Business Intelligence
41191.description: This undergraduate subject equips you with an understanding of business intelligence applications in organisational contexts, focusing on knowledge management, business process management, and decision-making. By taking this subject, you will gain valuable skills in generating, sharing, retaining, and applying information and knowledge within corporations, which are crucial for enhancing business efficiency and decision-making processes. You will develop essential skills in system development approaches and design strategies for business intelligence systems, preparing you for roles in business analysis and system design. These skills will not only help you become proficient in managing business processes but also make you an asset in any organisational setting that relies on data-driven decision-making. Your learning experience will be interactive and practical. Through engaging in case studies, project-based tasks, and group activities, you will apply theoretical knowledge to real-world business issues using different analytical tools. As you handle data sets, you'll improve your skills in analysing and implementing solutions. This practical approach ensures that you not only grasp the theoretical concepts but also become proficient in using these tools to effectively address and resolve business challenges.
learningOutcomes: Analyse Indigenous knowledge systems and practices as examples of cultural information systems. (A.1)
Assess ethical considerations in decision-making processes and practices for a business intelligence system in a real organisation. (B.1)
Design business intelligence applications to add value and competitive advantage in an organisation. (C.1)
Apply business intelligence and analytics tools to solve real-world problems and interpret results. (D.1)
Actively engage in and lead collaborative efforts within the business intelligence domain (E.1)

41193.title: IS Data Visualisation Studio
41193.description:
Taking the Information Systems (IS) perspective, rather than the more common Data Science or IT perspectives, this subject focuses on the latest developments and professional practices in data visualisation and visual analytics for non-technical decision-makers. Recognising the importance of data visualisation literacy in various disciplines, including IS, this subject stands out by emphasising (i) understanding the reasons behind using data visualisation in addition to learning how to create them, (ii) identifying business and organisational cases along with their requirements, stakeholders, and problem space, (iii) visual ethics and the responsible use of visual data, and (iv) utilising commercial data visualisation software instead of elaborate coding.

In short, the subject aims for visual problem exploration “through data” rather than the creation of static visual outputs. To achieve this, you will be taught through a combination of lectures and studios with a focus on design thinking exercises and ethical visual analytics. You will develop the necessary skills and mindset for problem finding and solving through visual data exploration that goes beyond creating static visual outputs. These skills include identifying different stakeholders and analysing their decision-making needs and environments, problem formulation, finding and ethically harvesting relevant data, ensuring data quality, data integration, multidimensional modelling, and developing a data exploration prototype using commercial data visualisation software.

Focusing on value creation and the decision-making needs of different stakeholders, you will also learn how to use data-driven visual storytelling and other contemporary techniques to explore the problem space, inform, influence, and inspire various types of stakeholders, including those in business and IT.
learningOutcomes: Determine the value proposition of data visualisation and visual data exploration for different decision-makers in an enterprise context. (B.1)
Integrate relevant data sources in an ethical manner following contemporary data quality and data integration principles and practice in an enterprise context. (D.1)
Design a prototype of a data exploration environment as an information system. (C.1)
Work collaboratively to design a data exploration prototype for a real-world problem. (E.1)
Reflect on the experience of becoming a competent, ethical and holistic data visualisation professional in an enterprise context. (F.1)

41201.title: Designing Sustainable Engineering Projects
41201.description: In this subject, you'll advance from foundational design principles to completing a full design cycle, from problem identification to presenting solutions to a client, incorporating systems thinking. Sustainability is central, encompassing environmental, economic, and social aspects, and you'll apply relevant tools and techniques within a group project themed by the coordinator, such as food or energy security. You'll work in teams, rotating roles to explore different sustainability perspectives, integrating feedback to refine your approach. Researching individually and in team, you'll converge to select appropriate sustainability frameworks and design a solution mindful of various factors, culminating in a professionally framed report.
learningOutcomes: Identify social, environmental, and economic needs and constraints for a project using sustainability frameworks, methods and tools. (B.1)
Apply systems thinking approaches to design solutions in complex projects. (C.1)
Apply relational teamwork skills to successfully complete a group project. (E.1)
Reflect on experiences to inform lifelong learning. (F.1)

41759.title: Capstone
41759.description:
The Capstone Project is a culminating subject undertaken by final-year students, designed to integrate and apply the knowledge, skills, and methodologies acquired throughout their degree program. Students work to deliver a substantial, research-informed, or industry-based project that addresses a complex real-world problem, opportunity, or area of interest within their discipline.

The project involves stages of problem identification, research, solution design, development, and evaluation. Many projects are delivered in collaboration with industry partners, research groups, or community organisations. It provides students with the opportunity to demonstrate independent thinking, technical competence, project management, and professional communication skills while producing a tangible outcome such as a prototype, software application, research report, or strategic proposal documented in a comprehensive final report.

It focuses on developing work-ready graduates with strong capabilities in independent research, creative problem-solving, innovation, and effective professional communication within the technology sector.
learningOutcomes: Integrate socially responsible professional judgement by identifying, evaluating, and responding to the ethical, environmental, social, and economic consequences of IT decisions, consistent with sustainable and accountable practice. (B.1)

Design solutions to complex computing problems by applying systematic design processes, creativity, and established discipline specific methods within broader technical, organisational, and societal contexts. (C.1)
Apply discipline‑specific knowledge, tools, and analytical methods to complex technical problems and evaluate sound professional decision‑making across IT contexts. (D.1)
Communicate project intent, design decisions, and outcomes clearly and professionally to a range of stakeholders and contribute constructively to team‑based work. (E.1)
Critically reflect on the development of discipline relevant professional skills and knowledge. (F.1)

41801.title: Technical Direction for 3D Animation and Graphics Projects
41801.description: This subject prepares you to excel as a Technical Director in computer graphics, encompassing 3D animation, visualisation, VFX, and games production. Technical Directors craft tools, maintain software, and manage the production pipeline. They work in animation and VFX studios and in the games industry. You'll need robust coding skills and a fundamental knowledge of Python.
learningOutcomes: Facilitate improved processes and pipelines for computer graphics projects. (C.1)
Able to identify requirements and prioritise tasks with regard to the production process, team workloads, and social and ethical considerations. (D.1)
Develop and configure animation and VFX pipeline tools to improve production efficiency. (D.1)
Contribute constructively to collaborative team dynamics and projects, enhancing the overall output through technical direction. (E.1)

41889.title: Application Development in the iOS Environment
41889.description: This subject introduces you to iOS application development, focusing on the Swift programming language and the iOS development environment. You'll gain practical experience with iOS app frameworks through hands-on software development exercises.
learningOutcomes: Design a well-structured programming solution that satisfies given software requirements. (C.1)
Implement the solution using Swift programming language under the iOS development environment. (D.1)
Independently explore and utilise various iOS frameworks and APIs. (D.1)
Demonstrate the fully tested software using iOS simulator for iPads and iPhones. (D.1)
41889.recommended: It is recommended that students have completed a programming subject, particularly 31251 Data Structures and Algorithms, prior to enrolling in the subject.

41890.title: Applying Network Security
41890.description: In this subject, you will delve into the theory behind computer security and apply it practically, drawing on content from the Network Security course provided by the Cisco Academy. You'll focus on network security appliances and infrastructure, including firewalls, access control, secure network design, Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), and data encryption, to build a robust understanding of protecting digital networks.
learningOutcomes: Describe the theoretical aspects of computer security with an in-depth focus on modern network security threats. (D.1)
Design, configure, test, manage, monitor and support network security infrastructure devices. (C.1)
Apply network security theory into practice using industry based techniques, processes and standards. (D.1)
Apply practical skills learnt in the labs to real-world commercial equipment and to prepare themselves for a industry based certification exam. (D.1)

41900.title: Cryptography
41900.description: In this subject, you will delve into the critical role of cryptographic techniques in maintaining data confidentiality and ensuring data integrity. These techniques are foundational in cybersecurity, securing a variety of systems such as wireless networks, online payment systems, and cryptocurrencies. You will explore key principles of cryptography, including both symmetric and asymmetric ciphers, cryptographic hash functions, message authentication codes, and digital signatures. Additionally, this subject introduces you to the popular applications of cryptography, such as the cryptographic designs in blockchain. Through hands-on exercises, you will analyse various cryptographic techniques, use popular cryptographic tools, and practise simulated attacks on cryptographic systems.
learningOutcomes: Explain the architectural principles, mathematical theories and key designs of underlying cryptographic algorithms. (D.1)
Implement cryptographic techniques and tools to prevent data interception and modification. (D.1)
Demonstrate system design principles and programmatic practices that lead to secure software systems. (C.1)
Work as an effective member of development teams. (E.1)
41900.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have completed 35010 Foundation Mathematics or equivalent.

41905.title: Software Defined Networks
41905.description: This subject addresses the demand for skilled network engineers in Software Defined Networking (SDN), a framework poised to meet the scalability and extensibility challenges of modern telecommunication networks. You will learn key SDN concepts and Network Function Virtualisation (NFV), and through hands-on labs, you will develop applications over an SDN controller. The subject equips you with the skills to enhance performance in data centres and enterprise networks, preparing you for industry needs.
learningOutcomes: Design, program, simulate and implement Software Defined Networking applications. (C.1)
Differentiate and evaluate Software Defined Networking Architectures, Controller Environments, Application Programming Interfaces and Platforms. (D.1)
Use tools for modelling Software Defined Networks. (D.1)
Use case scenarios to explain Network Function Virtualisation technologies, applications and benefits. (D.1)
Present project investigation, design and implementation to technical and lay audience. (E.1)
41905.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge of Unix-like operating systems; Python programming.

42028.title: Deep Learning and Convolutional Neural Network
42028.description: This subject delves into deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), highlighting their practical applications in data analytics, image recognition, and object detection. You'll study deep learning architectures, focusing on end-to-end model training for tasks like image classification. Practical sessions include setting up deep learning libraries, fine-tuning networks, and training your own CNNs on GPUs. You'll also learn model deployment to build an AI system. The coursework involves individual comprehension of cutting-edge research and collaborative projects to implement image classification and object detection systems.
learningOutcomes: Compare and contrast latest trends in Deep Learning strategies with traditional machine learning techniques. (D.1)
Build, train and test basic Convolutional Neural Networks for real image classification projects. (D.1)
Use Deep Learning software tools to explore state-of-the-art techniques and applications. (D.1)
Build, train and test customised object detection systems using Deep CNN-based techniques. (D.1)
Collaboratively develop the analysis, design and implementation of solutions to real-world computer vision problems. (C.1, E.1)

42028.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have basic knowledge of statistics and probability; Python programming.

42035.title: Cloud Security
42035.description: This subject explores the fundamentals of security, privacy, and trust in cloud computing, a paradigm that underpins most digital applications/services. Through the subject, you'll learn and apply these principles, designing secure, trustworthy cloud-based solutions on real-life platforms like AWS or Azure. Through project-based learning and industry-standard security risk analysis, you'll acquire the skills to assess, design, and implement security solutions for trustworthy cloud-based applications, gaining a deep understanding of the critical aspects of cloud system security.
learningOutcomes: Analyse security risks and threats in cloud and cloud applications with reference to government regulations and industry best practice. (B.1)
Design secure defence mechanisms for cloud applications encompassing the security domains of infrastructure, platform, application, data and privacy. (C.1)
Implement security mechanisms for securing cloud applications to minimise risk and threats in a cloud system/service. (D.1)

42036.title: Cybersecurity for Mobile Platforms
42036.description: This subject delves into the security risks and emerging threats associated with modern mobile devices and their operating systems. You'll explore platform security models, beginning with an introduction to the Android Studio simulation environment. The subject covers mobile platform security, encryption and decryption of messages, and mobile hardware security. You'll examine enterprise security extensions and conduct SQL mobile data injection, enhancing your understanding of data vulnerabilities. The subject also includes a comprehensive study of iOS security, covering hardware, system, application, service, and network security. Through practice-based learning, including secure data handling using AES and digital signatures, you will gain hands-on experience. The subject concludes with a review and recap of cybersecurity for mobile platforms, ensuring a well-rounded understanding of the field.
learningOutcomes: Analyse the current cybersecurity issues and challenges for the development of security solutions in mobile platforms. (B.1)
Apply practical security tools and technologies to design appropriate solutions for specific mobile platforms. (C.1)
Examine security risks to prevent fraud from mobile systems, services and applications. (D.1)

42037.title: IoT Security
42037.description: This subject introduces you to the Internet of Things (IoT), focusing on the security challenges and solutions associated with IoT devices and networks. You'll start with an introduction to IoT security and the Contiki software environment. The subject covers a range of critical topics, including implementing IPv6 on IoT devices, authentication methods, and ReST CoAP communications, all through hands-on labs using Contiki. You will explore IoT forensic techniques, hardware security, and data security and privacy concerns, learning practical skills like security port scanning, packet crafting, and Bluetooth sniffing. The subject delves into IoT malware, smart home security, and web application vulnerabilities, providing a comprehensive view of the threats and defenses in the IoT ecosystem. Through industry-relevant projects, you will build secure IoT systems, addressing real-world security challenges and enhancing your ability to protect IoT devices and networks. The subject concludes with a review and recap of IoT security principles, ensuring you have a solid foundation to create a secure and reliable digital ecosystem.
learningOutcomes: Understand the current cybersecurity issues and challenges for the development security solutions in IoT networks. (B.1)
Design IoT applications that incorporate practical security tools and technologies. (C.1)
Develop and implement secured solutions using a simulated environment such as Contiki in a team environment. (D.1)

42050.title: SAS Predictive Business Analytics
42050.description: Predictive business analytics is used to predict unknown future events by analysing historical business data and plays a critical function in data-driven business. This subject will equip you with the theoretical and practical foundations of predictive business analytics. You will comprehend analytical methods for business problem solving encompassing the entire predictive analytics lifecycle, from understanding business problems to deploying predictive models in the real-time business environment via case studies. This understanding will be further enhanced via demonstrations and hands-on exercises. You will use Model Studio in SAS Viya to develop and compare advanced analytics models, learning to create supervised machine learning models for informed decision-making with big data. The subject uses no code technology while setting you up to potentially achieve SAS Certified Specialist: Machine Learning Using SAS Viya certification.
learningOutcomes: Explore and transform business data into analytic-ready features for predictive modelling. (D.1)
Design and implement predictive models for predicting unknown future events in business environment. (C.1)
Evaluate and deploy predictive models in business production environment. (D.1)
Communicate effectively in a collaborative environment to explain and justify a design solution. (E.1)

args.scope: spk(s): C04379 - Master of Business Analytics (Extension)

42172.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
42172.description: This subject provides a grounding in Artificial Intelligence (AI), covering core areas such as learning, natural language processing, computer vision, search, knowledge representation, and reasoning. Through lectures/workshops and labs, you'll gain conceptual understanding of basic AI techniques and practical experience of using AI techniques and tools. You will be assessed in a knowledge test, a set of simple AI applications, and a group project designing an AI solution for a real-world problem, developing sound judgement and competence in this cutting-edge field.
learningOutcomes: Describe key ideas and applications of common AI techniques to people in the same discipline. (D.1)
Apply common AI algorithms to solve simple real-world problems. (D.1)

43010.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence and Incident Response
43010.description:
Cyber threat intelligence involves gathering and analysing information about potential cyber threats and risks from a range of sources. It helps organisations understand the tactics used by malicious actors and enables them to proactively identify and mitigate cyber threats.

Incident response is a structured process that empowers organisations to identify and address cybersecurity incidents and encompasses various stages, including preparing, preventing, detecting, analysing, containing, eliminating, and recovering from cyber-attacks or security breaches. It involves preparing for potential incidents, promptly detecting incidents and assessing the impact of the incidents, containing and eliminating the threat, recovering systems and data, and learning from the experience to enhance future incident response capabilities.

This subject brings these two concepts together by equipping students with the skills and knowledge to both prepare for, and respond to, cyber-attacks in organisational contexts. Through industry case studies and practical exercises, students will develop their abilities to proactively defend against cyber threats, mitigate risks, and strategically respond to incidents.
learningOutcomes: Identify social, environmental, economic and ethical aspects of Security Operations (SecOps). (B.1)
Design a strategy for cyber threat intelligence and incident response that reflects contemporary research and industry practice. (C.1)
Analyse cyber threat intelligence from various sources to detect and respond to contemporary cyber incidents. (D.1)
Demonstrate the ability to respond appropriately to simulated cybersecurity incidents in a security operations (SecOps) context. (D.1)
43010.recommended: It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have sound knowledge of computer networking; knowledge of internet security vulnerabilities and defences at the network and application level; awareness of security operations (SecOps) concepts.

43011.title: Industrial Control System Security
43011.description: This professional subject equips you with skills to protect critical infrastructures, like Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and Operational Technology (OT), from cyber threats. You will learn to identify vulnerabilities, assess risks, and implement security measures, including secure architectures and access controls. Your learning will be practical, involving lab exercises and real-world case studies, enabling you to defend against cyber-attacks on essential critical infrastructure systems.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate key concepts in Industrial Automation to apply standards architecture in industry. (D.1)
Apply various ICS security frameworks and standards to ensure security and to manage the industrial control system. (D.1)
Analyse cyber threats and attack vectors to identify the vulnerabilities of ICS controls and enhance security in different scenarios. (D.1)

43023.title: Emerging Topics in Artificial Intelligence
43023.description: This subject offers an introduction to current trends in artificial intelligence (AI), covering areas like autonomous machine learning, large language models, and natural language processing. Ideal for those keen on AI research or application development, you'll gain a broad understanding and deep expertise in a specific AI topic through a project mentored by UTS researchers. 43025.title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
43025.description:
This subject introduces quantum computation, a model of computation based on the physical laws of quantum mechanics. Quantum computers outperform traditional computers for a range of practical problems, and in many cases offer drastic advantages. In this subject, you will learn about the basic tools for understanding quantum information processing. You will apply this knowledge to study the key quantum protocols: teleportation, superdense coding, and simple quantum algorithms.

The subject covers key features of quantum theory which differentiate it from classical theory, including quantum entanglement and coherence.
learningOutcomes: Analyse quantum information protocols using the basic mathematical structure of quantum mechanics, including states, operations and measurements to validate performance claims. (D.1)
Design and create quantum circuits for quantum algorithms to run on quantum computers. (D.1)
Critically reflect and contrast the historical development of quantum and classical computation to differentiate computational capabilities. (D.1)
Effectively communicate quantum concepts to broad audiences. (E.1)

48024.description: This subject teaches concepts, theories and technologies underlying the methods and techniques of OOP programming and GUI programming.
